def plot_spectral_contagion_network(
    adjacency: pd.DataFrame | np.ndarray,
    branching_matrix: pd.DataFrame | np.ndarray | None = None,
    asset_names: list[str] | None = None,
    edge_threshold: float = 0.05,
    theme: ThemeName | str = "alloq_dark",
    title: str = "Spectral Laplacian Contagion Network & Fiedler Partition",
) -> go.Figure:
    """
    Visualizes the market topology as a two-panel Plotly figure:
    - Left Panel: Interactive graph network where node colors encode the Fiedler vector (v_2)
      spectral bisection partition (+ vs -), node sizes encode Hawkes self-/cross-excitation
      out-degree (systemic transmitter intensity), and edge thickness encodes partial-correlation
      coupling strength.
    - Right Panel: Sorted Fiedler vector (v_2) coordinates and systemic transmitter scores
      alongside algebraic connectivity (lambda_2) and Hawkes branching spectral radius (rho(G)).
    """
    palette = get_theme(theme)

    if isinstance(adjacency, pd.DataFrame):
        names = [str(c) for c in adjacency.columns]
        adj_mat = adjacency.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64, copy=True)
    else:
        adj_mat = np.asarray(adjacency, dtype=np.float64).copy()
        n = adj_mat.shape[0]
        names = (
            [str(a) for a in asset_names]
            if asset_names is not None and len(asset_names) == n
            else [f"Asset_{i}" for i in range(n)]
        )

    n = adj_mat.shape[0]
    adj_mat = 0.5 * (adj_mat + adj_mat.T)
    adj_mat = np.maximum(adj_mat, 0.0)
    np.fill_diagonal(adj_mat, 0.0)

    deg = adj_mat.sum(axis=1)
    inv_sqrt_deg = np.where(deg > 1e-12, 1.0 / np.sqrt(np.maximum(deg, 1e-12)), 0.0)
    d_half = np.diag(inv_sqrt_deg)
    lap = np.eye(n, dtype=np.float64) - d_half @ adj_mat @ d_half
    lap = 0.5 * (lap + lap.T)

    if n >= 2:
        evals, evecs = sla.eigh(lap)
        order = np.argsort(evals)
        evals = evals[order]
        evecs = evecs[:, order]
        lambda_2 = float(max(0.0, evals[1]))
        fiedler_vec = evecs[:, 1].astype(np.float64)
        if float(np.dot(fiedler_vec, np.arange(1, n + 1, dtype=np.float64))) < 0.0:
            fiedler_vec = -fiedler_vec
    else:
        lambda_2 = 1.0
        fiedler_vec = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.float64)

    if branching_matrix is not None:
        g_mat = np.asarray(branching_matrix, dtype=np.float64)
        out_influence = np.sum(np.abs(g_mat), axis=0)
        eigs_g = sla.eigvals(g_mat)
        rho_g = float(np.max(np.abs(eigs_g))) if len(eigs_g) > 0 else 0.0
    else:
        out_influence = deg.copy()
        rho_g = 0.0

    fig = make_subplots(
        rows=1,
        cols=2,
        column_widths=[0.58, 0.42],
        horizontal_spacing=0.10,
        subplot_titles=(
            f"Topology & Fiedler Cut (λ₂ = {lambda_2:.3f}, ρ(G) = {rho_g:.3f})",
            "Spectral Fiedler Coordinates (v₂) & Systemic Out-Degree",
        ),
    )

    # Circular layout ordered by Fiedler coordinate so clusters group naturally
    fiedler_order = np.argsort(fiedler_vec)
    angles = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.float64)
    for rank, node_idx in enumerate(fiedler_order):
        angles[node_idx] = 2.0 * np.pi * float(rank) / max(1, n)
    xs = np.cos(angles)
    ys = np.sin(angles)

    max_w = float(np.max(adj_mat)) if n > 1 and float(np.max(adj_mat)) > 1e-12 else 1.0
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            w = float(adj_mat[i, j])
            if w < edge_threshold:
                continue
            rel_w = float(np.clip(w / max_w, 0.15, 1.0))
            fig.add_trace(
                go.Scatter(
                    x=[xs[i], xs[j], None],
                    y=[ys[i], ys[j], None],
                    mode="lines",
                    line={
                        "width": 1.0 + 4.5 * rel_w,
                        "color": hex_to_rgba(palette.cyan, 0.25 + 0.55 * rel_w),
                    },
                    hoverinfo="skip",
                    showlegend=False,
                ),
                row=1,
                col=1,
            )

    max_inf = (
        float(np.max(out_influence)) if float(np.max(out_influence)) > 1e-12 else 1.0
    )
    node_sizes = 20.0 + 26.0 * (out_influence / max_inf)
    node_colors = [
        palette.emerald if float(v) >= 0.0 else palette.coral for v in fiedler_vec
    ]

    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=xs,
            y=ys,
            mode="markers+text",
            text=names,
            textposition="top center",
            marker={
                "size": node_sizes,
                "color": node_colors,
                "line": {"width": 2.0, "color": palette.bg_primary},
            },
            customdata=np.column_stack([fiedler_vec, out_influence]),
            hovertemplate=(
                "<b>%{text}</b><br>"
                "Fiedler v₂: %{customdata[0]:.4f}<br>"
                "Systemic Out-Degree: %{customdata[1]:.4f}<extra></extra>"
            ),
            name="Assets (Fiedler Cut)",
            showlegend=False,
        ),
        row=1,
        col=1,
    )

    sorted_names = [names[idx] for idx in fiedler_order]
    sorted_v2 = fiedler_vec[fiedler_order]
    sorted_colors = [
        palette.emerald if float(v) >= 0.0 else palette.coral for v in sorted_v2
    ]

    fig.add_trace(
        go.Bar(
            x=sorted_v2,
            y=sorted_names,
            orientation="h",
            marker={"color": sorted_colors},
            name="Fiedler Coordinate (v₂)",
            hovertemplate="<b>%{y}</b><br>v₂ = %{x:.4f}<extra></extra>",
        ),
        row=1,
        col=2,
    )

    fig.update_xaxes(
        visible=False, range=[-1.35, 1.35], showgrid=False, zeroline=False, row=1, col=1
    )
    fig.update_yaxes(
        visible=False, range=[-1.35, 1.35], showgrid=False, zeroline=False, row=1, col=1
    )
    fig.update_xaxes(title_text="Fiedler Vector Coordinate (v₂)", row=1, col=2)

    apply_plotly_theme(fig, theme=theme, title=title, height=520)
    return fig

def apply_plotly_theme(
    fig: Any,
    theme: ThemeName | str = "alloq_dark",
    title: str | None = None,
    subtitle: str | None = None,
    height: int | None = None,
    width: int | None = None,
) -> Any:
    """
    Applies the institutional PyAlloq layout styling to a Plotly Figure or Matplotlib Figure.
    """
    palette = get_theme(theme)

    # Check if fig is a Plotly Figure (duck-typed via update_layout)
    if hasattr(fig, "update_layout"):
        title_text = title
        if title and subtitle:
            title_text = (
                f"<b>{title}</b><br>"
                f"<span style='font-size:12px;color:{palette.text_secondary}'>{subtitle}</span>"
            )
        elif title:
            title_text = f"<b>{title}</b>"

        layout_kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {
            "paper_bgcolor": palette.bg_primary,
            "plot_bgcolor": palette.bg_secondary,
            "font": {
                "family": "Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif",
                "color": palette.text_primary,
                "size": 12,
            },
            "colorway": list(palette.categorical),
            "margin": {"l": 60, "r": 40, "t": 80 if title_text else 45, "b": 55},
            "hovermode": "x unified",
            "legend": {
                "bgcolor": hex_to_rgba(
                    palette.bg_card if palette.name == "alloq_dark" else "#FFFFFF", 0.8
                ),
                "bordercolor": palette.border_color,
                "borderwidth": 1,
                "font": {"color": palette.text_primary, "size": 11},
            },
        }
        if title_text is not None:
            layout_kwargs["title"] = {
                "text": title_text,
                "x": 0.02,
                "xanchor": "left",
                "font": {"size": 17, "color": palette.text_primary},
            }
        if height is not None:
            layout_kwargs["height"] = height
        if width is not None:
            layout_kwargs["width"] = width

        fig.update_layout(**layout_kwargs)
        fig.update_xaxes(
            gridcolor=palette.grid_color,
            zerolinecolor=palette.border_color,
            linecolor=palette.border_color,
            tickfont={"color": palette.text_secondary},
            title_font={"color": palette.text_primary},
        )
        fig.update_yaxes(
            gridcolor=palette.grid_color,
            zerolinecolor=palette.border_color,
            linecolor=palette.border_color,
            tickfont={"color": palette.text_secondary},
            title_font={"color": palette.text_primary},
        )
        # Update subplot titles if present
        if hasattr(fig.layout, "annotations") and fig.layout.annotations:
            for ann in fig.layout.annotations:
                if hasattr(ann, "font") and ann.font is not None and not ann.font.color:
                    ann.font.color = palette.text_primary
        return fig

    # Matplotlib Figure fallback
    if isinstance(fig, plt.Figure):
        fig.patch.set_facecolor(palette.bg_primary)
        for ax in fig.axes:
            ax.set_facecolor(palette.bg_secondary)
            ax.tick_params(colors=palette.text_secondary)
            ax.xaxis.label.set_color(palette.text_primary)
            ax.yaxis.label.set_color(palette.text_primary)
            ax.title.set_color(palette.text_primary)
            for spine in ax.spines.values():
                spine.set_edgecolor(palette.border_color)
            ax.grid(True, color=palette.border_color, alpha=0.3, linestyle="--")
        if title:
            fig.suptitle(
                title, color=palette.text_primary, fontsize=14, fontweight="bold"
            )
        return fig

    return fig

def hex_to_rgba(hex_color: str, alpha: float = 1.0) -> str:
    """Converts a 6-digit hex string (e.g. '#10B981') into an 'rgba(r, g, b, a)' string."""
    h = hex_color.lstrip("#")
    if len(h) == 3:
        h = "".join(c * 2 for c in h)
    r, g, b = int(h[0:2], 16), int(h[2:4], 16), int(h[4:6], 16)
    return f"rgba({r}, {g}, {b}, {alpha:.3f})"

Computes probability-weighted quantiles along 1D or 2D arrays. If values is 2D of shape (M, T), computes quantiles across axis=0 for each step t=0..T-1, returning an array of shape (len(quantiles), T).

Source code in src/pyalloq-viz/src/pyalloq_viz/utils.py 
def weighted_quantiles(
    values: np.ndarray,
    quantiles: list[float] | np.ndarray,
    sample_weight: np.ndarray | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Computes probability-weighted quantiles along 1D or 2D arrays.
    If `values` is 2D of shape (M, T), computes quantiles across axis=0 for each step t=0..T-1,
    returning an array of shape (len(quantiles), T).
    """
    q_arr = np.asarray(quantiles, dtype=np.float64)
    vals = np.asarray(values, dtype=np.float64)

    if sample_weight is None:
        return np.quantile(vals, q_arr, axis=0)

    weights = np.asarray(sample_weight, dtype=np.float64)
    weights = weights / np.sum(weights)

    if vals.ndim == 1:
        sorter = np.argsort(vals)
        v_sorted = vals[sorter]
        w_sorted = weights[sorter]
        cdf = np.cumsum(w_sorted) - 0.5 * w_sorted
        cdf = np.clip(cdf / cdf[-1], 0.0, 1.0)
        return np.interp(q_arr, cdf, v_sorted)

    if vals.ndim == 2:
        _M, T = vals.shape
        out = np.zeros((len(q_arr), T), dtype=np.float64)
        for t in range(T):
            col = vals[:, t]
            sorter = np.argsort(col)
            v_sorted = col[sorter]
            w_sorted = weights[sorter]
            cdf = np.cumsum(w_sorted) - 0.5 * w_sorted
            cdf = np.clip(cdf / cdf[-1], 0.0, 1.0)
            out[:, t] = np.interp(q_arr, cdf, v_sorted)
        return out

    raise ValueError("`values` must be 1D or 2D.")

Source code in src/pyalloq-viz/src/pyalloq_viz/utils.py 
def compute_kde_1d(
    values: np.ndarray,
    weights: np.ndarray | None = None,
    n_points: int = 250,
    padding: float = 0.1,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """
    Computes a smooth 1D Kernel Density Estimate (supporting scenario probability weights).
    """
    vals = np.asarray(values, dtype=np.float64)
    mask = np.isfinite(vals)
    vals = vals[mask]
    if len(vals) < 2 or np.std(vals) < 1e-12:
        center = float(np.mean(vals)) if len(vals) > 0 else 0.0
        x_grid = np.linspace(center - 0.05, center + 0.05, n_points)
        y_grid = np.exp(-0.5 * ((x_grid - center) / 0.01) ** 2)
        return x_grid, y_grid

    vmin, vmax = float(np.min(vals)), float(np.max(vals))
    span = max(vmax - vmin, 1e-6)
    x_grid = np.linspace(vmin - padding * span, vmax + padding * span, n_points)

    w_clean = None
    if weights is not None:
        w_arr = np.asarray(weights, dtype=np.float64)[mask]
        if np.sum(w_arr) > 0:
            w_clean = w_arr / np.sum(w_arr)

    try:
        kde = gaussian_kde(vals, weights=w_clean)
        y_grid = kde(x_grid)
    except (ValueError, np.linalg.LinAlgError):
        hist, bin_edges = np.histogram(
            vals, bins=min(30, max(5, len(vals) // 5)), weights=w_clean, density=True
        )
        centers = 0.5 * (bin_edges[:-1] + bin_edges[1:])
        y_grid = np.interp(x_grid, centers, hist, left=0.0, right=0.0)

    return x_grid, y_grid

Source code in src/pyalloq-viz/src/pyalloq_viz/utils.py 
def extract_equity_paths(
    source: MonteCarloResult | ScenarioMarketData | pd.DataFrame | np.ndarray,
    asset_weights: np.ndarray | pd.Series | None = None,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, pd.Index]:
    """
    Extracts a 2D array of portfolio equity paths of shape (M, T_steps) and corresponding timestamps
    from a MonteCarloResult, ScenarioMarketData, DataFrame, or ndarray.
    """
    if isinstance(source, MonteCarloResult):
        # equity_curves in MonteCarloResult has shape (T, M) where columns are Path_0..Path_M-1
        df_eq = source.equity_curves
        return df_eq.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64).T, df_eq.index

    if isinstance(source, ScenarioMarketData):
        _M, _T, N = source.prices.shape
        if asset_weights is None:
            w = np.full(N, 1.0 / N, dtype=np.float64)
        elif isinstance(asset_weights, pd.Series):
            w = (
                asset_weights.reindex(source.asset_names)
                .fillna(0.0)
                .to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
            )
        else:
            w = np.asarray(asset_weights, dtype=np.float64)

        if np.sum(np.abs(w)) > 0:
            w = w / np.sum(w)

        if source.initial_prices is not None:
            init_p = np.asarray(source.initial_prices, dtype=np.float64)[None, None, :]
            rel_prices = source.prices.astype(np.float64) / init_p
            step_wealth = np.asarray(
                np.tensordot(rel_prices, w, axes=([2], [0])), dtype=np.float64
            )  # (M, T)
        else:
            step_rets = np.tensordot(
                source.returns.astype(np.float64), w, axes=([2], [0])
            )
            step_wealth = np.asarray(
                np.cumprod(1.0 + step_rets, axis=1), dtype=np.float64
            )

        return step_wealth, source.timestamps

    if isinstance(source, pd.DataFrame):
        # Convention: if columns start with "Path" or index is DatetimeIndex, shape is (T, M)
        if isinstance(source.index, pd.DatetimeIndex) or any(
            str(c).startswith("Path") or str(c).startswith("CPCV")
            for c in source.columns
        ):
            return source.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64).T, source.index
        return source.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64), source.columns

    arr = np.asarray(source, dtype=np.float64)
    if arr.ndim != 2:
        raise ValueError("Equity paths array must be 2D of shape (M, T).")
    return arr, pd.RangeIndex(arr.shape[1])

Source code in src/pyalloq-viz/src/pyalloq_viz/utils.py 
def compute_drawdown_paths(equity_paths: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Computes underwater drawdown trajectories of shape (M, T) from equity paths of shape (M, T).
    Prepends 1.0 peak so initial drops below 1.0 are captured accurately.
    """
    eq = np.asarray(equity_paths, dtype=np.float64)
    running_peaks = np.maximum.accumulate(np.maximum(eq, 1.0), axis=1)
    drawdowns = (eq - running_peaks) / np.maximum(running_peaks, 1e-12)
    return drawdowns

Computes Capital Weight, Marginal Risk Contribution (MRC), Component Risk Contribution (CRC), and Percentage Component Risk Contribution (PCRC) for a portfolio.

Source code in src/pyalloq-viz/src/pyalloq_viz/utils.py 
def compute_risk_contributions(
    weights: pd.Series | np.ndarray,
    cov_matrix: pd.DataFrame | np.ndarray,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Computes Capital Weight, Marginal Risk Contribution (MRC), Component Risk Contribution (CRC),
    and Percentage Component Risk Contribution (PCRC) for a portfolio.
    """
    if isinstance(cov_matrix, pd.DataFrame):
        assets = list(cov_matrix.columns)
        Sigma = cov_matrix.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
    else:
        Sigma = np.asarray(cov_matrix, dtype=np.float64)
        assets = [f"Asset_{i}" for i in range(Sigma.shape[0])]

    if isinstance(weights, pd.Series):
        w = weights.reindex(assets).fillna(0.0).to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
    else:
        w = np.asarray(weights, dtype=np.float64)

    port_var = float(w.T @ Sigma @ w)
    port_vol = float(np.sqrt(max(port_var, 1e-16)))

    sigma_w = Sigma @ w
    mrc = sigma_w / port_vol
    crc = w * mrc
    pcrc = crc / port_vol if port_vol > 1e-12 else np.zeros_like(w)

    return pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "weight": w,
            "mrc": mrc,
            "crc": crc,
            "pcrc": pcrc,
        },
        index=assets,
    )

reconstruct_drifted_weights(
    backtest_result: BacktestResult | DataFrame,
    market_data: MarketData | DataFrame | None = None,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.Series]

Reconstructs true intra-period drifted asset weights and rebalance turnover events. When market_data (or asset prices DataFrame) is provided, simulates natural market drift: w_{i, t}^- = w_{i, t-1}^+ * (1 + r_{i, t}) / sum_j w_{j, t-1}^+ * (1 + r_{j, t}) and snaps back to target weights on dates where the target allocation changes. Returns: (drifted_weights_df, turnover_series)

Source code in src/pyalloq-viz/src/pyalloq_viz/utils.py 
def reconstruct_drifted_weights(
    backtest_result: BacktestResult | pd.DataFrame,
    market_data: MarketData | pd.DataFrame | None = None,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.Series]:
    """
    Reconstructs true intra-period drifted asset weights and rebalance turnover events.
    When `market_data` (or asset prices DataFrame) is provided, simulates natural market drift:
        w_{i, t}^- = w_{i, t-1}^+ * (1 + r_{i, t}) / sum_j w_{j, t-1}^+ * (1 + r_{j, t})
    and snaps back to target weights on dates where the target allocation changes.
    Returns:
        (drifted_weights_df, turnover_series)
    """
    if isinstance(backtest_result, BacktestResult):
        if (
            getattr(backtest_result, "target_weights", None) is not None
            and backtest_result.target_weights is not None
        ):
            target_w = backtest_result.target_weights.dropna(how="all").fillna(0.0)
        else:
            target_w = backtest_result.weights.dropna(how="all").fillna(0.0)
    else:
        target_w = backtest_result.dropna(how="all").fillna(0.0)

    if len(target_w) == 0:
        return target_w.copy(), pd.Series(dtype=float)

    prices_df: pd.DataFrame | None = None
    if isinstance(market_data, MarketData):
        prices_df = market_data.prices
    elif isinstance(market_data, pd.DataFrame):
        prices_df = market_data

    # Identify rebalance dates where target weights change (or first valid date)
    w_diff = target_w.diff().abs().sum(axis=1)
    rebalance_mask = (w_diff > 1e-7) | (np.arange(len(target_w)) == 0)

    if prices_df is None:
        turnover = w_diff.where(rebalance_mask, 0.0)
        return target_w.copy(), turnover

    common_dates = target_w.index.intersection(prices_df.index)
    if len(common_dates) < 2:
        turnover = w_diff.where(rebalance_mask, 0.0)
        return target_w.copy(), turnover

    target_aligned = target_w.loc[common_dates]
    asset_rets = (
        prices_df.reindex(columns=target_aligned.columns)
        .pct_change()
        .reindex(common_dates)
        .fillna(0.0)
    )
    reb_aligned = rebalance_mask.loc[common_dates]

    T, N = target_aligned.shape
    drifted_arr = np.zeros((T, N), dtype=np.float64)
    turnover_arr = np.zeros(T, dtype=np.float64)

    target_np = target_aligned.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
    rets_np = asset_rets.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
    reb_np = reb_aligned.to_numpy(dtype=bool)

    current_w = target_np[0].copy()
    drifted_arr[0] = current_w
    turnover_arr[0] = float(np.sum(np.abs(current_w)))

    for t in range(1, T):
        # Drift weights by day t's asset returns
        grown = current_w * (1.0 + rets_np[t])
        total_val = float(np.sum(grown))
        pre_rebalance_w = grown / total_val if total_val > 1e-12 else current_w

        if reb_np[t]:
            # Snap back to new target weights
            new_target = target_np[t]
            turnover_arr[t] = float(np.sum(np.abs(new_target - pre_rebalance_w)))
            current_w = new_target.copy()
        else:
            current_w = pre_rebalance_w

        drifted_arr[t] = current_w

    drifted_df = pd.DataFrame(
        drifted_arr, index=common_dates, columns=target_aligned.columns
    )
    turnover_series = pd.Series(turnover_arr, index=common_dates, name="Turnover")
    return drifted_df, turnover_series

docs.title: Building Blocks
docs.text:
PyAlloq is built around six composable building blocks. Each one has a clean, stable interface. You can swap any block independently without touching the others.

This design lets you answer questions like:

"Does Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage improve my Markowitz backtest?" "Does James-Stein return estimation help HRP more than EWMA?" "What happens if I use Almgren-Chriss costs instead of flat fees?"

...all without rewriting your backtesting code.

docs.title: The Six Blocks
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    subgraph INPUT["📡 Input"]
        DC["Data Connector\nBaseDataConnector"]
    end

    subgraph DATA["📦 Data Layer"]
        MD["MarketData\n(prices, features, rf_rate)"]
    end

    subgraph ESTIMATION["🔬 Estimation Layer"]
        RE["Return Estimator\nBaseReturnEstimator"]
        CE["Covariance Estimator\nBaseCovarianceEstimator"]
    end

    subgraph ALLOCATION["⚖️ Allocation Layer"]
        SP["StrategyPipeline"]
        AL["Allocator\nBaseAllocator"]
    end

    subgraph BACKTEST["🔁 Simulation Layer"]
        BE["WalkForwardEngine"]
        SP2["Splitter\nBaseWindowSplitter"]
        CM["Cost Model\nBaseCostModel"]
    end

    subgraph OUTPUT["📋 Output"]
        TS["TearSheet\nReturns / Weights"]
    end

    DC --> MD
    MD --> RE
    MD --> CE
    RE --> SP
    CE --> SP
    AL --> SP
    SP --> BE
    SP2 --> BE
    CM --> BE
    BE --> TS

docs.title: Block 1: Data Connector
docs.text:
Package: pyalloq-data-connector

Fetches raw data from any vendor and normalizes it into a MarketData object. Every connector wraps a different API but returns the same output.

from pyalloq_data_connector.yahoo_finance import YahooFinanceClient

data = YahooFinanceClient().get_market_data(
    tickers=["AAPL", "MSFT", "GOOGL"],
    start="2022-01-01",
    end="2024-01-01",
)

Available connectors: Yahoo Finance, Alpha Vantage, Finnhub, EOD Historical Data.

docs.title: Block 2: MarketData
docs.text:
Package: pyalloq-core

MarketData is the universal data container passed between all blocks. It holds:

Field Type Description prices pd.DataFrame Daily closing prices (rows = dates, cols = assets) features dict[str, pd.DataFrame] Time-series features: volume, macro, technicals, etc. cross_sectional pd.DataFrame \| None Market caps, sector mappings, etc. risk_free_rate pd.Series \| float Constant or time-varying risk-free rate risk_aversion pd.Series \| float 0 = most aggressive, 1 = most conservative

Zero-Lookahead Guarantee

MarketData.validate_alignment() raises an error if any feature index doesn't perfectly align with the price index. MarketData.slice_time(end_date, lookback) creates a safe time-window slice for each backtest period, preventing future data from leaking into the estimation window.

docs.title: Block 3: Return Estimator
docs.text:
Interface: BaseReturnEstimator.estimate(data: MarketData) -> pd.Series

Produces a pd.Series of annualized expected returns, one per asset. Plug any estimator into StrategyPipeline.

Estimator When to use MeanHistoricalReturnEstimator Arithmetic or geometric (CAGR) sample mean returns EWMAReturnEstimator Recent returns matter more (default) VolatilityScaledMultiHorizonEstimator / ResidualMomentumEstimator Cross-sectional & idiosyncratic momentum signals CAPMReturnEstimator / MultiFactorReturnEstimator Factor-model attribution (CAPM / Fama-French style) JamesSteinReturnEstimator Shrinkage — great for large asset universes ImpliedReturnEstimator Reverse-optimization from known market weights BlackLittermanReturnEstimator Blend market equilibrium with investor views inside StrategyPipeline

docs.title: Block 4: Covariance Estimator
docs.text:
Interface: BaseCovarianceEstimator.estimate(data: MarketData) -> pd.DataFrame

Produces an NxN covariance matrix. The choice of estimator significantly affects optimizer stability.

Estimator When to use EmpiricalCovariance Large T/N ratio, stable markets EWMACovariance Recent volatility clusters matter LedoitWolfEstimator Small sample, high-dimensional portfolios RandomMatrixTheoryEstimator Remove noise eigenvalues, detect true factors SemiCovariance Focus on downside risk only

docs.title: Block 5: Allocator
docs.text:
Interface: BaseAllocator.allocate(data, cov_matrix, expected_returns) -> OptimizationResult

Solves for optimal portfolio weights given the estimated inputs.

Classical (convex optimization via CVXPY):

Allocator Requires returns? EqualWeightAllocator, InverseVolatilityAllocator, MarketCapWeightAllocator No MarkowitzAllocator For Max Sharpe / Max Return / Efficient Return / Efficient Risk MeanCVaRAllocator, CDaRAllocator Optional (for target return or utility) RiskParityAllocator No RiskBudgetingAllocator No (uses data.features["risk_budgets"]) MaxDiversificationAllocator No MultiPeriodMPCAllocator, StochasticScenarioMPCAllocator Yes (multi-horizon forecasts or scenarios)

Graph-based ML (hierarchical clustering, no matrix inversion):

Allocator Method HRPAllocator Hierarchical Risk Parity HERCAllocator Hierarchical Equal Risk Contribution NCOAllocator Nested Cluster Optimization

docs.title: Block 6: StrategyPipeline
docs.text:
Package: pyalloq-core

StrategyPipeline is the glue that connects your estimators and allocator into a single callable unit. The backtest engine only knows about StrategyPipeline — it doesn't care which estimator or allocator you've chosen.

from pyalloq_core.pipeline import StrategyPipeline

pipeline = StrategyPipeline(
    allocator=MyAllocator(tickers=...),
    returns_estimator=MyReturnEstimator(),   # optional, defaults to EWMA
    cov_estimator=MyCovarianceEstimator(),   # optional, defaults to Empirical
)

weights = pipeline.generate_weights(data)  # → pd.Series

docs.title: Block 7: WalkForwardEngine
docs.text:
Package: pyalloq-backtest

The engine runs your StrategyPipeline across rolling or expanding historical windows, applying transaction costs on each rebalance. It enforces the zero-lookahead guarantee by slicing MarketData before each pipeline call.

from pyalloq_backtest.engine import WalkForwardEngine

engine = WalkForwardEngine(
    pipeline=pipeline,
    rebalance_freq="ME",                  # monthly
    splitter=RollingWindowSplitter(252),  # 1-year lookback
    cost_model=FlatBpsCostModel(10.0),    # 10bps per trade
)

results = engine.run(data)
# → {"returns": pd.Series, "weights": pd.DataFrame, "tear_sheet": pd.DataFrame}

docs.title: Block 8: Monte Carlo Simulation & Entropy Pooling
docs.text:
Package: pyalloq-simulation & pyalloq-core

Generates 3D \((M, T, N)\) synthetic price and feature tensors (ScenarioMarketData), blends non-Gaussian return and volatility views via EntropyPooler, and executes WalkForwardEngine across all \(M\) paths in parallel via ParallelMonteCarloEngine.

from pyalloq_simulation import GARCHEVTCopulaGenerator
from pyalloq_core.engines import ParallelMonteCarloEngine

gen = GARCHEVTCopulaGenerator(nu=5.0)
gen.fit(data)

mc_engine = ParallelMonteCarloEngine(backtest_engine=engine, max_workers=4)
mc_result = mc_engine.run_batches(gen.generate_batches(n_paths=500, horizon=252, batch_size=100))

docs.title: How They Fit Together
docs.text:
Every portfolio optimization workflow in PyAlloq follows the same linear data flow:

Data Connector → MarketData → [Return Estimator + Covariance Estimator] → Allocator
                                         ↕ (via StrategyPipeline)
                              WalkForwardEngine [+ Splitter + Cost Model]
                                         ↓
                                     TearSheet

This separation of concerns means you can:

  • Change the data source without touching your estimators
  • Change estimators without touching your allocator
  • Change the allocator without touching the backtest engine
  • Change cost models or splitters without changing anything else

docs.title: MarketData
docs.text:
MarketData is the single source of truth for all financial data in PyAlloq. Every building block — estimators, allocators, the backtest engine — consumes and produces MarketData.

Understanding how it works is essential to avoiding look-ahead bias in backtesting.

docs.title: Data Fields
docs.text:
from pyalloq_core.data import MarketData
import pandas as pd

data = MarketData(
    prices=prices_df,                    # required: (T × N) closing prices
    features={"volume": volume_df},      # optional: time-series features
    cross_sectional=market_caps_df,      # optional: static cross-sectional data
    risk_free_rate=0.04,                 # constant or pd.Series
    risk_aversion=1.0,                   # 0 = aggressive, 1 = conservative
)
Field Type Required Description prices pd.DataFrame ✅ Closing prices. Rows = dates, Columns = ticker symbols assets list[str] Auto Auto-inferred from prices.columns if not provided features dict[str, pd.DataFrame] ❌ Named time-series feature matrices. Must share the same DatetimeIndex as prices cross_sectional pd.DataFrame \| None ❌ Cross-sectional data (e.g., market caps, sector labels). Not time-indexed risk_free_rate pd.Series \| float ❌ Annual risk-free rate. Defaults to 0.0 risk_aversion pd.Series \| float ❌ Used by MarkowitzAllocator for MAX_RETURN utility. Defaults to 1.0

docs.title: The Features Dictionary
docs.text:
features is a flexible dictionary of named pd.DataFrame matrices. Use it to attach any time-series signal to your market data:

data = MarketData(
    prices=prices_df,
    features={
        "volume":        volume_df,           # daily traded volume
        "momentum_12m":  momentum_df,         # 12-month momentum signals
        "risk_budgets":  risk_budget_df,      # per-asset risk budgets (for RiskBudgetingAllocator)
        "vix":           vix_df,              # macro features
    }
)

Risk Budgets

RiskBudgetingAllocator reads its target budgets from data.features["risk_budgets"]. This is the standard way to pass allocator-specific inputs through the pipeline.

Almgren-Chriss Cost Model

AlmgrenChrissCostModel requires data.features["volume"] to be set for calculating market impact costs.

docs.title: validate_alignment()
docs.text:
Called automatically at construction time. Raises a ValueError if any feature matrix's index does not exactly match prices.index. This prevents silent data misalignment bugs.

# This raises ValueError immediately — catching the bug at construction, not later
data = MarketData(
    prices=daily_prices,
    features={"macro": weekly_macro_df},  # ❌ weekly index ≠ daily index
)
# ValueError: Data misalignment: Feature: macro index does not perfectly match 'prices' index.

docs.title: slice_time(end_date, lookback)
docs.text:
Creates a new MarketData instance safely sliced up to (and including) end_date. The backtest engine calls this for every rebalance window.

# Inside WalkForwardEngine — what happens at each rebalance date:
window_data = data.slice_time(
    end_date=pd.Timestamp("2023-06-30"),
    lookback=252,  # use 1 year of history
)

# window_data.prices ends at 2023-06-30 — no future data leaks through
weights = pipeline.generate_weights(window_data)

slice_time slices all fields consistently: prices, all features, and risk_free_rate (if a Series). The cross_sectional field is passed through unchanged since it is not time-indexed.

docs.title: Working with MarketData Directly
docs.text:
You can generate returns from prices:

returns = data.prices.pct_change().dropna()

Or select a sub-universe:

us_data = MarketData(
    prices=data.prices[["AAPL", "MSFT", "GOOGL"]],
    risk_free_rate=data.risk_free_rate,
)

docs.title: Design Philosophy
docs.text:
MarketData is intentionally a dumb container, not a class with business logic. This design choice means:

  • All components receive the same type of input
  • There is one canonical data format — no per-component data munging
  • Time alignment is validated once at construction, not repeatedly inside each component
  • The backtest engine can slice the data safely without knowing what's inside it

docs.title: ScenarioMarketData (3D Synthetic Tensors)
docs.text:
For Monte Carlo simulation (pyalloq-simulation), ScenarioMarketData wraps 3D \((M, T, N)\) synthetic price, return, and exogenous feature tensors while providing a zero-copy bridge back to 2D MarketData per path:

from pyalloq_core.data import ScenarioMarketData

# Slice path m into a standard 2D MarketData instance compatible with WalkForwardEngine
path_data = scenario_data.get_path(path_idx=0, feature_pipeline=my_feature_pipeline)

# Compute full-horizon cumulative asset returns (M × N) anchored at t=0 initial_prices
cum_returns = scenario_data.get_cumulative_returns()
Field Type Shape Description prices np.ndarray (M, T, N) Simulated asset price paths returns np.ndarray (M, T, N) Simulated single-step asset returns asset_names list[str] (N,) Ordered ticker symbols initial_prices np.ndarray \| None (N,) \(t=0\) anchor prices from the end of historical data timestamps pd.Index (T,) Forward-projected DatetimeIndex (or RangeIndex) features dict[str, np.ndarray] (M, T, K) Jointly synthesized exogenous feature tensors

docs.title: Swapping Components
docs.text:
Because every component in PyAlloq implements a clean interface, you can swap any piece of the stack with a single line of code — without changing anything else.

This page shows side-by-side examples of the most common swaps.

docs.title: Swapping Covariance Estimators
docs.text:
The covariance estimator has the biggest impact on optimizer stability, especially for Markowitz-family allocators. Try each with the same pipeline and compare results.

Empirical (Default)Ledoit-Wolf ShrinkageRMT DenoisingSemi-Covariance 
from pyalloq.classical.estimators.covariance.empirical import EmpiricalCovariance
from pyalloq_core.pipeline import StrategyPipeline
from pyalloq.classical.optimizers.markowitz import MarkowitzAllocator
from pyalloq_core.enums import ObjectiveFunction

pipeline = StrategyPipeline(
    allocator=MarkowitzAllocator(tickers=data.assets, objective=ObjectiveFunction.MIN_VOLATILITY),
    cov_estimator=EmpiricalCovariance(),  # sample covariance — sensitive to outliers
)

from pyalloq.classical.estimators.covariance.ledoit_wolf import LedoitWolfShrinkage

pipeline = StrategyPipeline(
    allocator=MarkowitzAllocator(tickers=data.assets, objective=ObjectiveFunction.MIN_VOLATILITY),
    cov_estimator=LedoitWolfShrinkage(),  # analytically optimal shrinkage intensity
)

from pyalloq.classical.estimators.covariance.random_matrix_theory import RandomMatrixTheoryEstimator

pipeline = StrategyPipeline(
    allocator=MarkowitzAllocator(tickers=data.assets, objective=ObjectiveFunction.MIN_VOLATILITY),
    cov_estimator=RandomMatrixTheoryEstimator(denoise=True, detone=False),
)

from pyalloq.classical.estimators.covariance.semi_covariance import SemiCovariance

pipeline = StrategyPipeline(
    allocator=MarkowitzAllocator(tickers=data.assets, objective=ObjectiveFunction.MIN_VOLATILITY),
    cov_estimator=SemiCovariance(),  # penalizes downside volatility only
)

docs.title: Swapping Return Estimators
docs.text:
For allocators that use expected returns (Max Sharpe, Max Return, Black-Litterman), the choice of return estimator directly impacts weights.

EWMA (Default)James-Stein ShrinkageVolatility-Scaled MomentumResidual MomentumTimesFM 3.0 (Foundation Model)Timestral (Foundation Model)Implied Returns 
from pyalloq.classical.estimators.returns.classical.ewma import EWMAReturnEstimator

pipeline = StrategyPipeline(
    allocator=MarkowitzAllocator(tickers=data.assets, objective=ObjectiveFunction.MAX_SHARPE),
    returns_estimator=EWMAReturnEstimator(),  # exponentially weighted mean
)

from pyalloq.classical.estimators.returns.classical.james_stein import JamesSteinReturnEstimator

pipeline = StrategyPipeline(
    allocator=MarkowitzAllocator(tickers=data.assets, objective=ObjectiveFunction.MAX_SHARPE),
    returns_estimator=JamesSteinReturnEstimator(),  # shrinks towards grand mean
)

from pyalloq.classical.estimators.returns.classical.momentum import VolatilityScaledMultiHorizonEstimator

pipeline = StrategyPipeline(
    allocator=MarkowitzAllocator(tickers=data.assets, objective=ObjectiveFunction.MAX_SHARPE),
    returns_estimator=VolatilityScaledMultiHorizonEstimator(),  # multi-horizon volatility-scaled z-score
)

from pyalloq.classical.estimators.returns.classical.momentum import ResidualMomentumEstimator

pipeline = StrategyPipeline(
    allocator=MarkowitzAllocator(tickers=data.assets, objective=ObjectiveFunction.MAX_SHARPE),
    returns_estimator=ResidualMomentumEstimator(),  # beta-neutralized idiosyncratic momentum
)

from pyalloq.dl.estimators.returns.timesfm import TimesFM3MultivariateReturnEstimator
from timesfm3 import TimesFM3Evaluator

tfm_model = TimesFM3Evaluator.load_pretrained(...)  # Loaded TimesFM 3.0 evaluator

pipeline = StrategyPipeline(
    allocator=MarkowitzAllocator(tickers=data.assets, objective=ObjectiveFunction.MAX_SHARPE),
    returns_estimator=TimesFM3MultivariateReturnEstimator(model=tfm_model, horizon=21),
)

from pyalloq.dl import TimestralMultivariateReturnEstimator

pipeline = StrategyPipeline(
    allocator=MarkowitzAllocator(tickers=data.assets, objective=ObjectiveFunction.MAX_SHARPE),
    returns_estimator=TimestralMultivariateReturnEstimator(
        model="mistralai/Timestral-28M", horizon=21
    ),
)

from pyalloq.classical.estimators.returns.classical.implied import ImpliedReturnEstimator

pipeline = StrategyPipeline(
    allocator=MarkowitzAllocator(tickers=data.assets, objective=ObjectiveFunction.MAX_SHARPE),
    returns_estimator=ImpliedReturnEstimator(),  # reverse-optimization from market weights
)

docs.title: Swapping Allocators
docs.text:
The allocator is completely decoupled from estimators and the backtest engine. Swap it freely.

Risk ParityMarkowitz (Min Vol)HRP (Hierarchical Risk Parity)Max DiversificationEqual Weight (Baseline) 
from pyalloq.classical.optimizers.risk_parity import RiskParityAllocator

pipeline = StrategyPipeline(
    allocator=RiskParityAllocator(tickers=data.assets),
)

from pyalloq.classical.optimizers.markowitz import MarkowitzAllocator
from pyalloq_core.enums import ObjectiveFunction

pipeline = StrategyPipeline(
    allocator=MarkowitzAllocator(tickers=data.assets, objective=ObjectiveFunction.MIN_VOLATILITY),
)

from pyalloq.ml.optimizers.hrp import HRPAllocator

pipeline = StrategyPipeline(
    allocator=HRPAllocator(tickers=data.assets),
)

from pyalloq.classical.optimizers.max_diversification import MaxDiversificationAllocator

pipeline = StrategyPipeline(
    allocator=MaxDiversificationAllocator(tickers=data.assets),
)

from pyalloq.classical.optimizers.naive import EqualWeightAllocator

pipeline = StrategyPipeline(
    allocator=EqualWeightAllocator(tickers=data.assets),
)

docs.title: Swapping Backtest Splitters
docs.text:
The splitter controls how the engine partitions history for each rebalance window. Swap it in WalkForwardEngine.

Rolling Window (Default)Expanding Window 
from pyalloq_backtest.splitters import RollingWindowSplitter
from pyalloq_backtest.engine import WalkForwardEngine

engine = WalkForwardEngine(
    pipeline=pipeline,
    splitter=RollingWindowSplitter(lookback_window=252),  # fixed 1-year window
)

from pyalloq_backtest.splitters import ExpandingWindowSplitter

engine = WalkForwardEngine(
    pipeline=pipeline,
    splitter=ExpandingWindowSplitter(min_periods=252),  # grows with all available history
)

docs.title: Swapping Transaction Cost Models
docs.text:
Flat Bps (Default)Almgren-Chriss Market Impact 
from pyalloq_backtest.costs import FlatBpsCostModel

engine = WalkForwardEngine(
    pipeline=pipeline,
    cost_model=FlatBpsCostModel(bps=10.0),  # 10 basis points per trade
)

from pyalloq_backtest.costs import AlmgrenChrissCostModel

# Requires data.features["volume"] to be set
engine = WalkForwardEngine(
    pipeline=pipeline,
    cost_model=AlmgrenChrissCostModel(
        portfolio_aum=1_000_000,
        spread_bps=2.0,
        gamma=0.1,
    ),
)

docs.title: Comparing Strategies Side-by-Side
docs.text:
Run multiple pipelines through the same engine and collect results for comparison:

from pyalloq_backtest.engine import WalkForwardEngine

strategies = {
    "Equal Weight":   EqualWeightAllocator(tickers=data.assets),
    "Risk Parity":    RiskParityAllocator(tickers=data.assets),
    "HRP":            HRPAllocator(tickers=data.assets),
    "Min Volatility": MarkowitzAllocator(tickers=data.assets, objective=ObjectiveFunction.MIN_VOLATILITY),
}

results = {}
for name, allocator in strategies.items():
    pipeline = StrategyPipeline(allocator=allocator)
    engine = WalkForwardEngine(pipeline=pipeline, rebalance_freq="ME")
    results[name] = engine.run(data)

# Compare Sharpe ratios
for name, res in results.items():
    sharpe = res["tear_sheet"].loc["sharpe_ratio", "Value"]
    print(f"{name:<20} Sharpe: {sharpe:.2f}")

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: PyAlloq requires Python 3.11+.

docs.title: Using uv (Recommended)
docs.text:
uv is the recommended package manager for PyAlloq.

uv add pyalloq

To also install optional machine learning or deep learning extras:

# Deep learning (PyTorch-based models)
uv add "pyalloq[dl]"

# Reinforcement learning (Stable-Baselines3 + Gymnasium)
uv add "pyalloq[rl]"

# All ML extras
uv add "pyalloq[all-ml]"

docs.title: Using pip
docs.text:
pip install pyalloq

With optional extras:

pip install "pyalloq[dl]"
pip install "pyalloq[rl]"
pip install "pyalloq[all-ml]"

docs.title: Development Installation (from source)
docs.text:
Clone the repository and install all workspace packages together:

git clone https://github.com/AlloqAlpha/pyalloq.git
cd pyalloq

# Install all workspace packages + dev dependencies
uv sync --all-extras

This installs pyalloq, pyalloq-core, pyalloq-backtest, pyalloq-data-connector, pyalloq-features, pyalloq-simulation, and pyalloq-viz as editable workspace packages.

docs.title: Optional Dependencies
docs.text:
Extra Key packages Use case [dl] torch>=2.0, timesfm==3.0.1 Deep learning & foundation model estimators [rl] stable-baselines3, gymnasium Reinforcement learning allocators [all-ml] All of the above Full ML stack

To use Mistral AI's Timestral foundation models (TimestralUnivariateReturnEstimator, TimestralMultivariateReturnEstimator, TimestralUnivariateViewGenerator, TimestralMultivariateViewGenerator), install the standalone inference library from GitHub alongside pyalloq[dl]:

pip install git+https://github.com/mistralai/timestral.git

docs.title: Verify Installation
docs.text:

import pyalloq_simulation

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This guide walks you through building and backtesting a complete portfolio strategy end-to-end.

docs.title: Step 1 — Fetch Market Data
docs.text:
Use a data connector to download prices. All connectors return a standardized MarketData object.

from pyalloq_data_connector.yahoo_finance import YahooFinanceClient

client = YahooFinanceClient()
data = client.get_market_data(
    tickers=["AAPL", "MSFT", "GOOGL", "AMZN", "TSLA"],
    start="2020-01-01",
    end="2024-01-01",
)

print(data.assets)   # ['AAPL', 'MSFT', 'GOOGL', 'AMZN', 'TSLA']
print(data.prices.shape)  # (1006, 5)

docs.title: Step 2 — Choose an Allocator
docs.text:
Pick any allocator from pyalloq.classical.optimizers or pyalloq.ml.optimizers. Every allocator implements the same BaseAllocator interface.

from pyalloq.classical.optimizers.risk_parity import RiskParityAllocator

allocator = RiskParityAllocator(tickers=data.assets)

docs.title: Step 3 — Build a Strategy Pipeline
docs.text:
StrategyPipeline wires together your return estimator, covariance estimator, and allocator. Defaults are EWMA returns and empirical covariance.

from pyalloq_core.pipeline import StrategyPipeline

pipeline = StrategyPipeline(allocator=allocator)

To customize the estimators:

from pyalloq.classical.estimators.covariance.ledoit_wolf import LedoitWolfShrinkage
from pyalloq.classical.estimators.returns.classical.james_stein import JamesSteinReturnEstimator

pipeline = StrategyPipeline(
    allocator=allocator,
    returns_estimator=JamesSteinReturnEstimator(),
    cov_estimator=LedoitWolfShrinkage(),
)

docs.title: Step 4 — Run a Walk-Forward Backtest
docs.text:
WalkForwardEngine runs your pipeline on rolling windows of historical data, rebalancing at a specified frequency, and accounts for transaction costs.

from pyalloq_backtest.engine import WalkForwardEngine

engine = WalkForwardEngine(
    pipeline=pipeline,
    rebalance_freq="ME",  # Monthly rebalancing
)

results = engine.run(data)

docs.title: Step 5 — Inspect Results
docs.text:
The engine returns a dictionary with portfolio returns, daily weights, and a performance tear sheet.

print(results["tear_sheet"])

                       Value
total_return            1.23
annualized_return       0.21
annualized_volatility   0.14
sharpe_ratio            1.45
maximum_drawdown       -0.18
calmar_ratio            1.17

You can also access the raw returns and weight history:

portfolio_returns = results["returns"]     # pd.Series
weight_history    = results["weights"]     # pd.DataFrame

docs.title: Step 6 — Convert Continuous Weights into Integer Share Orders
docs.text:
When ready to execute live trades, use DiscreteShareAllocator to convert your latest target weights into exact integer share counts and residual cash:

from pyalloq import DiscreteShareAllocator

latest_weights = pipeline.generate_weights(data)
disc = DiscreteShareAllocator(total_portfolio_value=100_000.0)
allocation = disc.allocate(latest_weights, latest_prices=data, method="greedy")

print(allocation.shares)         # {'AAPL': 112, 'MSFT': 54, ...}
print(allocation.leftover_cash)  # Remaining uninvested cash

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
from pyalloq_data_connector.yahoo_finance import YahooFinanceClient
from pyalloq.classical.optimizers.risk_parity import RiskParityAllocator
from pyalloq.classical.estimators.covariance.ledoit_wolf import LedoitWolfShrinkage
from pyalloq_core.pipeline import StrategyPipeline
from pyalloq_backtest.engine import WalkForwardEngine

# 1. Fetch data
data = YahooFinanceClient().get_market_data(
    tickers=["AAPL", "MSFT", "GOOGL", "AMZN", "TSLA"],
    start="2020-01-01",
    end="2024-01-01",
)

# 2. Build pipeline
pipeline = StrategyPipeline(
    allocator=RiskParityAllocator(tickers=data.assets),
    cov_estimator=LedoitWolfShrinkage(),
)

# 3. Run backtest
results = WalkForwardEngine(pipeline=pipeline, rebalance_freq="ME").run(data)

# 4. Review performance
print(results["tear_sheet"])
