docs.title: Deflated Sharpe Ratio & Performance Attribution
docs.text: This page documents the mathematical foundations behind pyalloq-backtest's multiple-testing correction (BacktestTracker, MultiStrategyComparator, and the Deflated Sharpe Ratio) and 3-pillar active return decomposition (PerformanceAttributor).

docs.title: 1. The Multiple Testing Problem & Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR)
docs.text: When evaluating \(N\) candidate strategies or hyperparameter configurations on historical data, selecting the strategy with the highest sample Sharpe ratio \(\widehat{\text{SR}}\) introduces severe selection bias (the "Single-Path Illusion").

docs.title: Expected Maximum Sharpe Ratio (False Strategy Theorem)
docs.text:
Bailey & López de Prado (2014) prove via extreme value theory (Gumbel asymptotic distribution of Gaussian maxima) that across \(N \ge 2\) independent trials with cross-sectional Sharpe variance \(\text{Var}[\{\widehat{\text{SR}}_n\}]\) and null mean \(\mathbb{E}[\widehat{\text{SR}}_n] = \text{SR}_{\text{target}}\), the expected maximum Sharpe ratio under the null hypothesis of zero true skill is:

\[ \widehat{\text{SR}}_0 = \text{SR}_{\text{target}} + \sqrt{\text{Var}[\{\widehat{\text{SR}}_n\}]} \left( (1 - \gamma)\,\Phi^{-1}\!\left(1 - \frac{1}{N}\right) + \gamma\,\Phi^{-1}\!\left(1 - \frac{1}{N e}\right) \right) \]

where \(\gamma \approx 0.5772156649\) is the Euler-Mascheroni constant, \(e \approx 2.71828\), and \(\Phi^{-1}(\cdot)\) is the standard normal quantile function.

docs.title: Non-Normal Sharpe Estimator Variance & DSR
docs.text:
For a return series of length \(T\) with non-annualized sample Sharpe ratio \(\widehat{\text{SR}}\), sample skewness \(\hat{\gamma}_3\), and Pearson kurtosis \(\hat{\gamma}_4 = \hat{\kappa}_{\text{excess}} + 3\), Mertens (2002) and Bailey & López de Prado (2012, 2014) show that the asymptotic standard error of \(\widehat{\text{SR}}\) is:

\[ \hat{\sigma}(\widehat{\text{SR}}) = \sqrt{\frac{1 - \hat{\gamma}_3\,\widehat{\text{SR}} + \frac{\hat{\gamma}_4 - 1}{4}\,\widehat{\text{SR}}^2}{T - 1}} \]

The Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR) is the probability that the true Sharpe ratio exceeds the multiple-testing hurdle \(\widehat{\text{SR}}_0\):

\[ \text{DSR} = \Phi\!\left( \frac{(\widehat{\text{SR}} - \widehat{\text{SR}}_0)\sqrt{T - 1}}{\sqrt{1 - \hat{\gamma}_3\,\widehat{\text{SR}} + \frac{\hat{\gamma}_4 - 1}{4}\,\widehat{\text{SR}}^2}} \right) \in [0, 1] \]

When \(N = 1\), \(\widehat{\text{SR}}_0 = \text{SR}_{\text{target}}\) and DSR reduces to the Probabilistic Sharpe Ratio (PSR).

docs.title: 2. Classical Brinson-Fachler Decomposition
docs.text:
Given a universe of \(M\) assets partitioned into \(J\) disjoint sectors or hierarchical clusters \(\{S_1, \dots, S_J\}\) at period \(t\):

  • Portfolio cluster weight: \(w_{p,j,t} = \sum_{i \in S_j} w_{p,i,t}\)
  • Benchmark cluster weight: \(w_{b,j,t} = \sum_{i \in S_j} w_{b,i,t}\)
  • Portfolio within-cluster return: \(R_{p,j,t} = \sum_{i \in S_j} \frac{w_{p,i,t}}{w_{p,j,t}} r_{i,t}\)
  • Benchmark within-cluster return: \(R_{b,j,t} = \sum_{i \in S_j} \frac{w_{b,i,t}}{w_{b,j,t}} r_{i,t}\)
  • Total portfolio & benchmark return: \(R_{p,t} = \sum_{j=1}^J w_{p,j,t} R_{p,j,t}\), \(\; R_{b,t} = \sum_{j=1}^J w_{b,j,t} R_{b,j,t}\)

Brinson & Fachler (1985) decompose the single-period active return \(R_{p,t} - R_{b,t}\) into three orthogonal economic effects for each cluster \(j\):

\[ \begin{aligned} \text{Allocation Effect:} \quad A_{j,t} &= (w_{p,j,t} - w_{b,j,t})(R_{b,j,t} - R_{b,t}) \\ \text{Selection Effect:} \quad S_{j,t} &= w_{b,j,t}(R_{p,j,t} - R_{b,j,t}) \\ \text{Interaction Effect:} \quad I_{j,t} &= (w_{p,j,t} - w_{b,j,t})(R_{p,j,t} - R_{b,j,t}) \end{aligned} \]

Summing across all clusters \(j = 1, \dots, J\) satisfies the exact single-period identity:

\[ \sum_{j=1}^J \left( A_{j,t} + S_{j,t} + I_{j,t} \right) = R_{p,t} - R_{b,t} \]

docs.title: Carino (1999) Geometric Multi-Period Linking
docs.text:
Because geometric multi-period returns compound multiplicatively, \(R_p = \prod_{t=1}^T (1 + R_{p,t}) - 1\) and \(R_b = \prod_{t=1}^T (1 + R_{b,t}) - 1\), simple arithmetic sums of single-period attribution effects leave a compounding residual. Carino (1999) eliminates this residual via logarithmic linking coefficients:

\[ k_t = \frac{\ln(1 + R_{p,t}) - \ln(1 + R_{b,t})}{R_{p,t} - R_{b,t}}, \qquad K = \frac{\ln(1 + R_p) - \ln(1 + R_b)}{R_p - R_b} \]

with continuous limit \(k_t = \frac{1}{1 + R_{p,t}}\) when \(R_{p,t} = R_{b,t}\). Scaling each period's effect by \(k_t / K\) guarantees exact multi-period additivity:

\[ \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{j=1}^J \frac{k_t}{K}\left( A_{j,t} + S_{j,t} + I_{j,t} \right) = R_p - R_b \]

docs.title: 3. Factor-Implied Active Return Attribution
docs.text:
To test whether an allocator's active return \(y_t = R_{p,t} - R_{b,t}\) arises from genuine idiosyncratic skill (\(\alpha\)) or passive exposure to systematic risk premia \(F_t \in \mathbb{R}^K\) (e.g., Market, Size, Value, Momentum, Low-Volatility), PerformanceAttributor estimates the linear factor model:

\[ y_t = \alpha + \sum_{k=1}^K \beta_k F_{k,t} + \varepsilon_t \]

To account for serial correlation and conditional heteroscedasticity in daily portfolio returns, standard errors and \(t\)-statistics are computed using the Newey-West (1987) HAC covariance estimator with Bartlett kernel bandwidth \(L\):

\[ \widehat{\text{Cov}}_{\text{HAC}}(\hat{\theta}) = \frac{T}{T - K - 1}(X^\top X)^{-1} \widehat{S}_{\text{NW}} (X^\top X)^{-1} \]

where:

\[ \widehat{S}_{\text{NW}} = \sum_{t=1}^T \hat{\varepsilon}_t^2 x_t x_t^\top + \sum_{\ell=1}^L \left(1 - \frac{\ell}{L + 1}\right) \sum_{t=\ell+1}^T \hat{\varepsilon}_t \hat{\varepsilon}_{t-\ell}\left(x_t x_{t-\ell}^\top + x_{t-\ell} x_t^\top\right) \]

docs.title: 4. Frictional Drag Accounting (Ma & Smith, 2025)
docs.text:
In multi-period trading under alpha decay and convex market impact (Ma & Smith, 2025; Almgren & Chriss, 2001), the gap between a theoretical signal's paper return and net realized return decomposes into an exact additive bridge at each step \(t\):

  1. Theoretical Paper Return (\(R_{t}^{\text{paper}}\)): Return of un-drifted target weights \(w_t^*\): [ R_t^{\text{paper}} = (w_t^)^\top r_t + \max(0, 1 - \mathbf{1}^\top w_t^) r_{f,t} ]
  2. Alpha Decay & Intra-Period Drift Drag (\(\Delta_t^{\text{drift}}\)): Performance wedge between actual held weights \(w_t^{\text{held}}\) (subject to intra-period price drift and rebalance threshold gating) and theoretical target weights: [ \Delta_t^{\text{drift}} = R_t^{\text{gross}} - R_t^{\text{paper}} ]
  3. Proportional Spread & Commission Drag (\(C_t^{\text{spread}}\)): Linear \(\ell_1\) execution cost: [ C_t^{\text{spread}} = \sum_{i=1}^M c_{\text{spread}, i} |\Delta w_{i,t}| ]
  4. Square-Root Market Impact Drag (\(C_t^{\text{impact}}\)): Non-linear Almgren-Chriss price impact: [ C_t^{\text{impact}} = \sum_{i=1}^M \gamma_i \sqrt{\frac{\text{AUM} \cdot |\Delta w_{i,t}|}{V_{i,t}}} |\Delta w_{i,t}| ]
  5. Short Borrow Drag (\(C_t^{\text{borrow}}\)): Financing cost on short exposure \(\sum_i \max(0, -w_{i,t}^{\text{held}})\).

Combining all terms yields the exact Gross-to-Net Waterfall identity:

\[ R_t^{\text{net}} = R_t^{\text{paper}} + \Delta_t^{\text{drift}} - C_t^{\text{spread}} - C_t^{\text{impact}} - C_t^{\text{borrow}} \]

docs.title: Estimator Mathematics
docs.text: This page covers the mathematical foundations of the return and covariance estimators implemented in pyalloq.

docs.title: Exponentially Weighted Mean (EWMA)
docs.text:
Weights observations exponentially so that recent returns matter more:

\[ \hat{\mu}^{EWMA}_i = \frac{\sum_{t=1}^{T} \lambda^{T-t} r_{i,t}}{\sum_{t=1}^{T} \lambda^{T-t}} \]

where the decay factor \(\lambda = 1 - \frac{2}{\text{span}+1}\).

docs.title: James-Stein Shrinkage
docs.text:
Shrinks each asset's historical mean towards the grand mean of all assets. For \(N \geq 3\) assets, the James-Stein estimator strictly dominates the sample mean in terms of MSE:

\[ \hat{\mu}^{JS} = (1 - w^*) \hat{\mu} + w^* \bar{\mu} \mathbf{1} \]

The optimal shrinkage intensity \(w^*\) is:

\[ w^* = \min\left(1,\; \frac{N-2}{(\hat{\mu} - \bar{\mu}\mathbf{1})^\top \hat{\Sigma}^{-1} (\hat{\mu} - \bar{\mu}\mathbf{1})}\right) \]

where \(\bar{\mu} = \frac{1}{N}\sum_i \hat{\mu}_i\) is the grand mean.

docs.title: Implied Returns (Reverse Optimization)
docs.text:
Given observed market-capitalization weights \(w^{mkt}\) and the market risk aversion \(\lambda\), the implied equilibrium excess returns are:

\[ \Pi = \lambda \Sigma w^{mkt} \]

This is the equilibrium prior used in Black-Litterman.

docs.title: Black-Litterman
docs.text:
Combines the market equilibrium prior \(\Pi\) with investor views \((P, Q)\) through Bayesian updating.

Views: \(P \in \mathbb{R}^{K \times N}\) is a view-picking matrix, \(Q \in \mathbb{R}^K\) are the expected view returns, and \(\Omega\) is the uncertainty matrix for the views.

Posterior expected returns:

\[ \mu^* = \left[(\tau\Sigma)^{-1} + P^\top \Omega^{-1} P\right]^{-1} \left[(\tau\Sigma)^{-1} \Pi + P^\top \Omega^{-1} Q\right] \]

Posterior covariance:

\[ \Sigma^* = \Sigma + \left[(\tau\Sigma)^{-1} + P^\top \Omega^{-1} P\right]^{-1} \]

where \(\tau\) is a scalar controlling the uncertainty in the prior (typically 0.01–0.05).

docs.title: Ledoit-Wolf Shrinkage
docs.text:
Shrinks the sample covariance \(\hat{\Sigma}\) towards a structured target \(T\) (e.g., diagonal matrix):

\[ \hat{\Sigma}^{LW} = (1 - \alpha^*) \hat{\Sigma} + \alpha^* \hat{\mu}_{cov} I \]

The optimal shrinkage intensity \(\alpha^*\) is derived analytically by minimizing the Frobenius norm of the estimation error:

\[ \alpha^* = \frac{\delta^2}{\gamma^2} \]

where \(\delta^2\) and \(\gamma^2\) are data-dependent scaling constants derived from the Oracle Approximating Shrinkage (OAS) method.

See: Ledoit & Wolf (2004)

docs.title: Random Matrix Theory (Marchenko-Pastur)
docs.text:
For a random matrix \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{T \times N}\) with i.i.d. entries, the eigenvalue distribution of \(\hat{\Sigma} = \frac{1}{T} X^\top X\) converges to the Marchenko-Pastur distribution with upper bound:

\[ \lambda_+ = \sigma^2 \left(1 + \sqrt{\frac{N}{T}}\right)^2 \]

Any empirical eigenvalue \(\lambda_i < \lambda_+\) is attributable to noise, not signal. The denoising step replaces these with the average noise eigenvalue:

\[ \bar{\lambda}_{noise} = \frac{\sum_{i: \lambda_i < \lambda_+} \lambda_i}{|\{i: \lambda_i < \lambda_+\}|} \]

Then the clean covariance is reconstructed: \(\hat{\Sigma}^{RMT} = V \Lambda_{clean} V^\top\)

The optional detoning step removes the largest eigenvalue (corresponding to the market-wide factor) from the correlation matrix before reconstruction, isolating sector-level correlations.

docs.title: Semi-Covariance
docs.text:
Uses only negative return periods to estimate covariance, focusing on downside co-movement:

\[ \hat{\Sigma}^{semi}_{ij} = \frac{1}{T^-} \sum_{t: r_{i,t} < 0} r_{i,t} \cdot r_{j,t} \]

where \(T^-\) is the count of periods where asset \(i\) had a negative return.

docs.title: EWMA Covariance
docs.text:
Uses exponential weighting to capture time-varying covariance:

\[ \hat{\Sigma}_t = (1 - \lambda) r_t r_t^\top + \lambda \hat{\Sigma}_{t-1} \]

where \(\lambda = 1 - \frac{2}{\text{span}+1}\) is the decay factor. This models volatility clustering observed in financial time series (similar to the RiskMetrics model).

docs.title: Point-in-Time Model-Free Implied Volatility & Buss-Vilkov Implied Covariance
1. Model-Free Implied Volatility (PITOptionsMFIVTransformer)
docs.text:
Following Britten-Jones & Neuberger (2000) and the CBOE VIX methodology, the risk-neutral integrated variance over horizon \(\tau\) is extracted without assuming Black-Scholes dynamics by integrating out-of-the-money (OTM) option mid-prices \(Q_t(K_k, \tau)\) across strikes \(K_k\) strictly stamped prior to the decision cut-off (\(\text{quote\_timestamp} \le t\)):

\[ \sigma_{\text{MFIV}, i}^2(t, \tau) = \frac{2 e^{r \tau}}{\tau} \sum_{k} \frac{\Delta K_k}{K_k^2} Q_t(K_k, \tau) - \frac{1}{\tau} \left( \frac{F_{t,\tau}}{K_0} - 1 \right)^2 \]

docs.title: 2. Buss & Vilkov (2012) Option-Implied Correlation (ImpliedCovarianceEstimator)
docs.text:
Given the diagonal matrix of forward-looking implied volatilities \(D_{\text{IV}, t} = \operatorname{diag}(\sigma_{1,t}^{\text{IV}}, \dots, \sigma_{N,t}^{\text{IV}})\) and the Ledoit-Wolf shrunk physical correlation matrix \(\Gamma_t^{\text{hist}}\), the implied correlation matrix is parameterized as a convex shift toward the equicorrelation target \(\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^\top\):

\[ \Gamma_t^{\text{imp}} = (1 - \gamma_t) \Gamma_t^{\text{hist}} + \gamma_t \mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^\top, \qquad \hat{\Sigma}_t^{\text{imp}} = D_{\text{IV}, t} \, \Gamma_t^{\text{imp}} \, D_{\text{IV}, t} \]

When the index implied volatility \(\sigma_{M,t}^{\text{IV}}\) for market weights \(w_M \in \Delta^N\) is observed, \(\gamma_t\) is solved in closed form:

\[ \gamma_t = \frac{\left(\sigma_{M,t}^{\text{IV}}\right)^2 - w_M^\top D_{\text{IV}, t} \Gamma_t^{\text{hist}} D_{\text{IV}, t} w_M}{\left(w_M^\top \sigma_t^{\text{IV}}\right)^2 - w_M^\top D_{\text{IV}, t} \Gamma_t^{\text{hist}} D_{\text{IV}, t} w_M} \]

docs.title: Graph Reaction-Diffusion Covariance (ReactionDiffusionCovarianceEstimator)
docs.text:
Let \(\Theta_t = \left(\Gamma_t^{\text{LW}} + \varepsilon I_N\right)^{-1}\) denote the regularized precision matrix. The non-negative partial correlation adjacency matrix \(W_t\) and symmetric normalized Graph Laplacian \(\mathcal{L}_t\) are defined by:

\[ W_{ij, t} = \max\!\left(0, -\frac{\Theta_{ij, t}}{\sqrt{\Theta_{ii, t} \Theta_{jj, t}}}\right) \quad (i \neq j), \qquad \mathcal{L}_t = I_N - D_t^{-1/2} W_t D_t^{-1/2} \]

The normalized log-volatility excitation field \(v_t \in \mathbb{R}^N\) and slow liquidity inhibitor \(u_t \in \mathbb{R}^N\) evolve over horizon \(H\) via the coupled FitzHugh-Nagumo Graph Reaction-Diffusion system:

\[ \frac{dv}{dt} = -D_v \mathcal{L}_t v - \kappa_v v + \gamma_{\text{react}} \, v (v - \theta_{\text{crit}})(1 - v) - \beta_u u \] \[ \frac{du}{dt} = -D_u \mathcal{L}_t u + \epsilon_u (v - 0.8 u) \]

Integrating \((v_t, u_t)\) to \(t = H\) via 4th-order Runge-Kutta (RK4) yields the forward volatility vector \(\hat{\sigma}_i(H) = \bar{\sigma}_i \exp(v_i(H))\) and contagion-tightened correlation matrix \(\hat{\Gamma}_H\), forming \(\hat{\Sigma}_{t+H} = \operatorname{diag}(\hat{\sigma}(H)) \, \hat{\Gamma}_H \, \operatorname{diag}(\hat{\sigma}(H))\).

docs.title: Spectral Graph Fragility & Wiener-Hopf Multivariate Hawkes Process (SpectralGraphFragility, WienerHopfHawkesSolver)
docs.text:
1. Spectral Algebraic Connectivity (Fiedler Value \(\lambda_2\)): Let \(0 = \lambda_1 \le \lambda_2 \le \dots \le \lambda_N \le 2\) denote the eigenvalues of the symmetric normalized Graph Laplacian \(\mathcal{L}_t = I_N - D_t^{-1/2} W_t D_t^{-1/2}\). The Fiedler value \(\lambda_2(\mathcal{L}_t)\) measures algebraic connectivity and systemic cascade propensity, while \(\tau_{\text{mix}} = \lambda_2(\mathcal{L}_t)^{-1}\) defines the network mixing time and \(v_2 \in \mathbb{R}^N\) provides the optimal spectral bisection coordinate.

  2. Non-Parametric Wiener-Hopf Multivariate Hawkes Excitation (WienerHopfHawkesSolver): For the \(N\)-dimensional self-exciting jump point process \(\boldsymbol{\lambda}_t = \boldsymbol{\mu} + \int_0^t \boldsymbol{\Phi}(t - s) \, d\mathbf{N}_s\), the causal excitation kernels \(\Phi_{ij}(\tau)\) satisfy the coupled Wiener-Hopf integral system:

\[ C_{ij}(\tau) = \Lambda_j \Phi_{ij}(\tau) + \sum_{k=1}^N \int_0^\infty \Phi_{ik}(u) C_{kj}(\tau - u) \, du, \qquad \forall \tau > 0 \]

Discretizing over \(Q\) lag quadrature nodes yields a block-Toeplitz linear system whose solution determines the branching ratio matrix \(G = \|\boldsymbol{\Phi}\|_1 \in \mathbb{R}_+^{N \times N}\) and criticality spectral radius \(\rho(G) = \max_k |\lambda_k(G)| \in [0, 1)\).

docs.title: Markovian Lifted Heston Rough Volatility & Log-Signatures (LiftedHestonRoughVolTransformer, LogSignatureTransformer)
docs.text:
1. Lyndon-Basis Truncated Log-Signature: Over a local window \([s, t]\) of the time-augmented price-volatility path \(X_u = (u, \log P_u, \sigma_u)\), the depth-2 log-signature combines Level-1 increments \(\Delta X_{s,t}\) with the signed Lévy areas (Lie brackets):
\[ \mathcal{A}^{a,b}_{s,t} = \frac{1}{2} \int_s^t \left( (X_u^a - X_s^a)\,dX_u^b - (X_u^b - X_s^b)\,dX_u^a \right) \]

  1. Abi Jaber (2019) \(K\)-Factor Markovian Lifted Heston Kernel: Approximates the singular fractional power-law kernel \(K(t) = t^{H - 1/2} / \Gamma(H + 1/2)\) via a finite superposition of \(K\) Markovian Ornstein-Uhlenbeck volatility factors \(U_{t,k}\) with geometric mean-reversion speeds \(x_k = r^{k - K/2}\) and analytic weights \(c_k(H_{\text{eff}})\), where \(H_{\text{eff}} \in (0.05, 0.50]\) blends the realized variogram Hurst \(H_{\text{RV}}\) and implied surface Hurst \(H_{\text{IV}}\).

  2. Bakshi-Kapadia-Madan (2003) Risk-Neutral Moments & Cornish-Fisher Tail Expansion: From out-of-the-money (OTM) option prices \(Q(K_i)\), the quadratic (\(V\)), cubic (\(W\)), and quartic (\(X\)) model-free contracts determine risk-neutral skewness (\(\text{MFIS}_t\)) and excess kurtosis (\(\text{MFIK}_t\)). When use_cornish_fisher_tail=True, ImpliedCovarianceEstimator scales each asset's implied volatility by the Cornish-Fisher quantile ratio at confidence \(z_\alpha\):

\[ m_{\text{CF}}(S, K_{\text{ex}}) = \frac{z_{\text{CF}}}{z_\alpha}, \qquad z_{\text{CF}} = z_\alpha + \frac{z_\alpha^2 - 1}{6} S + \frac{z_\alpha^3 - 3 z_\alpha}{24} K_{\text{ex}} - \frac{2 z_\alpha^3 - 5 z_\alpha}{36} S^2 \]
  1. Von Neumann Covariance Entropy (compute_von_neumann_entropy): Given normalized eigenvalues \(p_i = \lambda_i(\Sigma) / \operatorname{Tr}(\Sigma)\), the normalized Von Neumann Entropy measures spectral diversification vs. rank-1 contagion collapse:
\[ \mathcal{S}_{\text{vN}}(\Sigma) = -\frac{1}{\ln N} \sum_{i=1}^N p_i \ln p_i \in [0, 1] \]

docs.title: Time-Aware Prior-Data Fitted Networks (ApolloPFN, Potapczynski et al., TMLR 2026)
docs.text:
1. Amortized In-Context Posterior Predictive Distribution (PPD): Trained offline on synthetic Structural Causal Model (SCM) time-series tasks \(\mathcal{D} \sim p(\mathcal{D})\) generated via Algorithm 1 (SRNGNPriorGenerator, Single Root Node Random Growing Network), ApolloPFNTransformer directly approximates the Bayesian posterior predictive distribution in a single forward pass:
\[ q_\theta\!\left(Y_{T+1:T+H} \;\middle|\; X_{1:T+H}, \, Y_{1:T}\right) \;\approx\; \int p\!\left(Y_{T+1:T+H} \mid X_{T+1:T+H}, \xi\right) p\!\left(\xi \mid X_{1:T}, Y_{1:T}\right) d\xi \]
  1. Temporal-Feature Factorized Transformer (AttnFeat + RoPE AttnSamp): Given embedding tensor \(Z \in \mathbb{R}^{(T+H) \times F \times D}\) with observation mask tokens \(0\) (observed) and \(-2\) (unobserved horizon targets) plus absolute sinusoidal encodings \(\Omega_{t, 2d}\), each layer \(\ell = 1, \dots, L\) alternates cross-variate attention and Rotary Position Embedded (RoPE) full-horizon temporal attention:
\[ Z \leftarrow \operatorname{LN}_1\!\left(Z + \operatorname{AttnFeat}(Z)\right), \quad Z \leftarrow \operatorname{LN}_2\!\left(Z + \operatorname{AttnSamp}_{\text{RoPE}}(Z)\right), \quad Z \leftarrow \operatorname{LN}_3\!\left(Z + \operatorname{MLP}(Z)\right) \]
  1. Riemann Bar Distribution & sCRPS-Adaptive Bayesian Model Averaging (EnsembleReturnEstimator): The output head parameterizes a piecewise-constant density over \(B\) Riemann bins spanning \([z_{\min}, z_{\max}]\). Evaluated across quantile levels \(\alpha_1 < \dots < \alpha_Q\), the scale-free Continuous Ranked Probability Score (sCRPS, Appendix B) is:
\[ \operatorname{sCRPS}(y, \hat{y}) = \frac{\sum_{t=T+1}^{T+H} \frac{2}{Q} \sum_{j=1}^Q \left[ \alpha_j \left(y_t - \hat{y}_t^{\alpha_j}\right)_+ + (1 - \alpha_j)\left(\hat{y}_t^{\alpha_j} - y_t\right)_+ \right]}{\sum_{t=T+1}^{T+H} |y_t|} \]

In EnsembleReturnEstimator, model \(m\)'s weight on asset \(i\) under weighting_mode="scrps_adaptive" is proportional to its calibrated precision \(w_{m,i} \propto \left(\sigma_{m,i}^2 \cdot \operatorname{sCRPS}_m\right)^{-1}\), or under weighting_mode="cvar_adaptive" to its inverse squared tail risk \(w_{m,i} \propto \operatorname{CVaR}_{\alpha, m, i}^{-2}\).

  1. Closed-Form Riemann Bar Tail Functionals & Copula-Coupled Scenario Generation (Müller et al., ICLR 2022; Demarta & McNeil, 2005; Patton, 2006): Given Riemann bin edges \(b_0 < b_1 < \dots < b_B\), widths \(w_k = b_{k+1} - b_k\), probabilities \(p_k\), and cumulative probabilities \(C_k = \sum_{j < k} p_j\), the truncated probability mass in bin \(k\) below tail threshold \(1 - \alpha\) is \(\Delta p_k = \max(0, \min(p_k, 1 - \alpha - C_k))\). With the Müller et al. (2022) half-normal left-tail shift \(\delta_0 = \sqrt{2/\pi} w_0\) on the outermost bucket \(k = 0\), RiemannBarDistribution evaluates exact Expected Shortfall (\(\operatorname{CVaR}_\alpha\)), Sortino downside semi-deviation (\(\sigma_{-}\)), and Bowley skewness (\(\mathcal{S}_{\text{Bowley}}\)):
\[ \operatorname{CVaR}_\alpha(Z) = -\frac{1}{1 - \alpha} \sum_{k=0}^{B-1} \Delta p_k \left(b_k + \frac{\Delta p_k}{2 p_k} w_k - \delta_0 \mathbb{I}_{\{k=0\}}\right), \qquad \mathcal{S}_{\text{Bowley}} = \frac{(q_{0.90} - q_{0.50}) - (q_{0.50} - q_{0.10})}{q_{0.90} - q_{0.10}} \]

To synthesize joint \(N\)-asset scenarios (BaseScenarioEstimator), correlated uniform variates \(u^{(m, h)} \sim C_{\nu, R_{\text{imp}}}^{\text{t}}\) are drawn from a Student-\(t\) (or stratified LHS-\(t\)) copula parameterized by the Buss & Vilkov (2012) option-implied correlation matrix blended with AttnFeat epistemic correlation, and inverted through each asset's exact Riemann Bar marginal CDF: \(\tilde{r}_{i, h}^{(m)} = \mu_{i,\text{ctx}} + \sigma_{i,\text{ctx}} F_{\text{bar}, i, h}^{-1}(u_i^{(m, h)})\).

docs.title: Permutation-Invariant Set Transformers & Equivariant Deep Covariance (SetTransformerCovarianceNet, SetTransformerPolicyNet)
docs.text:
1. Three Portfolio Symmetry Laws: Let \(X_t \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d}\) denote the cross-sectional matrix of per-asset temporal embeddings at decision time \(t\), and let \(\Pi \in \{0, 1\}^{N \times N}\) be any permutation matrix reordering tickers:
  2. Permutation Invariance (Global [REGIME] token \(z_{\text{regime}}\), cash logit \(l_t^{(\text{cash})}\), RL critic \(V_\psi(s_t)\), and latent factor covariance \(\Sigma_{F,t} \in \mathbb{S}_{++}^m\)): [ g(\Pi X_t) = g(X_t) \qquad \forall \Pi \in S_N ]
  3. 1D Permutation Equivariance (Expected returns \(\hat{\mu}_t\), factor loadings \(B_t \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times m}\), idiosyncratic variances \(d_t \in \mathbb{R}_{++}^N\), and portfolio weights \(w_t \in \mathbb{R}^N\)): [ f(\Pi X_t) = \Pi f(X_t) \qquad \forall \Pi \in S_N ]

  4. 2D Congruence Equivariance (Cross-asset covariance matrix \(\hat{\Sigma}_t \in \mathbb{S}_{++}^N\)): [ \hat{\Sigma}(\Pi X_t) = \Pi \hat{\Sigma}(X_t) \Pi^\top \qquad \forall \Pi \in S_N ]

  5. Induced Set Attention Blocks (ISAB), Pooling by Multihead Attention (PMA), and Scalable-Softmax (SSMax): Following Lee et al. (ICML 2019), ISAB replaces quadratic \(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\) pairwise self-attention (SAB) with \(m \ll N\) learnable inducing points \(I \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times d}\) functioning as dynamic latent risk factors: [ H_{I,t} = \operatorname{MAB}1(I, X_t) \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times d}, \qquad Z_t = \operatorname{MAB}_2(X_t, H, \qquad z_{\text{regime}, t} = \operatorname{PMA}}) \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d1(Z_t) = \operatorname{MAB}(S, \operatorname{rFF}(Z_t)) ] To eliminate Softmax attention fading when transferring from a 500-stock training universe to a 50-stock inference sleeve, every variable-cardinality attention key axis replaces standard Softmax with Scalable-Softmax (Nakanishi, 2025) over active tradable assets \(N_{\text{active}} = \sum_{j=1}^N m_{j,t}\): [ \operatorname{SSMax}(z_i; N ]}}, s) = \frac{m_{i,t} \exp!\left((s \ln N_{\text{active}})\, z_i\right)}{\sum_{j=1}^N m_{j,t} \exp!\left((s \ln N_{\text{active}})\, z_j\right)

  6. Three Strictly Congruence-Equivariant PSD Covariance Heads:

  7. ISAB Low-Rank Factor-Plus-Diagonal Head (ISABFactorDiagonalHead, head_type="factor_diag"): Reuses both the equivariant asset embeddings \(Z_t\) and the invariant inducing-point factor state \(H_{I,t}\): [ \hat{\Sigma}t = B_t \Sigma B_t^\top + D_t, \qquad B_t = \phi_B(Z_t) \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times m}, \quad D_t = \operatorname{diag}!\left(\operatorname{softplus}(\phi_D(Z_t)) + \epsilon_d\right), \quad \Sigma_{F,t} = \frac{1}{d} H_{I,t} H_{I,t}^\top + \epsilon_F I_m ]
  8. Volatility-Scaled Equivariant Gram Correlation Head (EquivariantGramCorrHead, head_type="gram_corr"): Maps each asset to \(\ell_2\)-normalized row vectors \(\tilde{u}_{i,t} = u_{i,t} / (\|u_{i,t}\|_2 + \epsilon)\) blended with learnable [REGIME] shrinkage \(\lambda_t \in (0, 1)\): [ \hat{\Gamma}t = (1 - \lambda_t) \tilde{U}_t \tilde{U}_t^\top + \lambda_t I_N, \qquad \hat{\Sigma}_t = D} \hat{\Gammat D ]

  9. Rotation- and Permutation-Invariant Spectral Cleaning (RIESpectralHead, head_type="rie_spectral", Bongiorno et al., 2026): Decomposes the sample correlation matrix \(C_t = V_t \Lambda_t V_t^\top\), passes the unordered eigenvalue set \(\{(\lambda_{k,t}, q_{\text{in}})\}\) with aspect ratio \(q_{\text{in}} = N_{\text{active}} / L\) through a 1D equivariant Set Attention block to predict cleaned eigenvalues \(\lambda_t^*\), and recombines \(\hat{\Sigma}_t = D_{\sigma, t} (V_t \operatorname{diag}(\lambda_t^*) V_t^\top) D_{\sigma, t}\).

  10. Exact \(\mathcal{O}(N m^2 + m^3)\) Woodbury Inversion & Cardinality-Normalized Losses (WoodburyGaussianNLLLoss, WoodburySteinLoss): Via the Woodbury Matrix Identity and Matrix Determinant Lemma with capacitance matrix \(M_t = \Sigma_{F,t}^{-1} + B_t^\top D_t^{-1} B_t \in \mathbb{S}_{++}^m\): [ \hat{\Sigma}t^{-1} v = D_t^{-1} v - D_t^{-1} B_t M_t^{-1} B_t^\top D_t^{-1} v, \qquad \ln |\hat{\Sigma}_t| = \sum| + \ln |M_t| ] Normalizing Gaussian NLL and James-Stein loss by }} \ln d_{i,t} + \ln |\Sigma_{F,t\(N_{\text{active}}\) holds loss magnitudes and gradient norms invariant across mixed-cardinality batches.

docs.title: Graph-Based Allocator Mathematics
docs.text:
This page covers the mathematical foundations of the hierarchical clustering-based allocators: HRP, HERC, and NCO.

These methods avoid inverting the covariance matrix, making them more numerically stable for large universes and ill-conditioned matrices.

docs.title: Hierarchical Risk Parity (HRP)
docs.text: López de Prado (2016). HRP uses hierarchical clustering on the correlation matrix to build a tree of related assets, then allocates weights top-down through the tree using inverse-variance weighting.

docs.title: Step 1: Distance Matrix
docs.text:
Convert the correlation matrix \(\rho\) into a metric distance matrix:

\[ d_{ij} = \sqrt{\frac{1 - \rho_{ij}}{2}} \]

Properties: \(d_{ii} = 0\), \(d_{ij} = d_{ji}\), \(0 \leq d_{ij} \leq 1\).

docs.title: Step 2: Hierarchical Clustering (Dendrogram)
docs.text:
Apply single-linkage agglomerative clustering to the distance matrix to build a binary tree (dendrogram). At each merge step, the distance between two clusters is:

\[ d(C_1, C_2) = \min_{i \in C_1, j \in C_2} d_{ij} \]

docs.title: Step 3: Quasi-Diagonalization
docs.text: Re-order the assets (leaves of the dendrogram) such that similar assets are adjacent. The resulting reordering makes the covariance matrix approximately block-diagonal.

docs.title: Step 4: Recursive Bisection
docs.text:
Traverse the dendrogram top-down. At each level, split the current cluster into two sub-clusters and allocate capital inversely proportional to their sub-portfolio variances:

\[ w_{left} \leftarrow w_{left} \times \alpha, \quad w_{right} \leftarrow w_{right} \times (1 - \alpha) \]

where the allocation split \(\alpha\) is:

\[ \alpha = 1 - \frac{\tilde{\sigma}^2_{left}}{\tilde{\sigma}^2_{left} + \tilde{\sigma}^2_{right}} \]

and \(\tilde{\sigma}^2_C\) is the variance of the inverse-variance portfolio of cluster \(C\):

\[ \tilde{w}_i = \frac{1/\sigma^2_i}{\sum_{j \in C} 1/\sigma^2_j}, \quad \tilde{\sigma}^2_C = \tilde{w}^\top_C \Sigma_C \tilde{w}_C \]

docs.title: Spectral Graph Laplacian HRP (SpectralLaplacianHRPAllocator)
docs.text:
Instead of single-linkage agglomerative clustering, Spectral Graph Laplacian HRP recursively partitions any induced subgraph \(S \subseteq V\) using the Fiedler vector \(v_2(\mathcal{L}_S)\) (the eigenvector corresponding to the second smallest eigenvalue \(\lambda_2(\mathcal{L}_S)\) of \(\mathcal{L}_S = I - D_S^{-1/2} W_S D_S^{-1/2}\)):

  1. Cheeger Conductance Sweep Cut: Sort nodes \(i \in S\) by their Fiedler coordinate \(v_{2,i}(\mathcal{L}_S)\) and select the split index \(s^*\) minimizing the regularized Cheeger normalized cut conductance \(\phi(S_L, S_R)\).
  2. Fragility-Tilted Recursive Bisection: Modify each sub-cluster's effective variance by its internal algebraic connectivity \(\lambda_2(\mathcal{L}_{S_c})\):
\[ \tilde{V}_{S_c} = \tilde{\sigma}^2_{S_c} \left(1 + \eta_{\text{frag}} \, \lambda_2(\mathcal{L}_{S_c})\right), \qquad \alpha = 1 - \frac{\tilde{V}_{S_L}}{\tilde{V}_{S_L} + \tilde{V}_{S_R}} \]

docs.title: Differentiable Risk Parity KKT Layer (DifferentiableRiskParityLayer)
docs.text:
By Spinu's (2013) convex log-barrier formulation of Risk Budgeting / Risk Parity:

\[ y^*(\hat{\Sigma}, b) = \arg\min_{y > 0} \frac{1}{2} y^\top \hat{\Sigma} y - \sum_{i=1}^N b_i \ln y_i, \qquad w^* = \frac{y^*}{\mathbf{1}^\top y^*} \]

the KKT stationarity condition \(F(y^*, \hat{\Sigma}, b) = \hat{\Sigma} y^* - b / y^* = \mathbf{0}\) has an exact closed-form positive-definite Jacobian \(J_y = \hat{\Sigma} + \operatorname{diag}(b / (y^*)^2)\), enabling exact implicit differentiation without unrolling Newton iterations:

\[ \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}_{\text{task}}}{\partial \hat{\Sigma}} = -\frac{1}{2}\left(u (y^*)^\top + y^* u^\top\right), \qquad \text{where } \left(\hat{\Sigma} + \operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac{b}{(y^*)^2}\right)\right) u = \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}_{\text{task}}}{\partial y^*} \]

docs.title: Hierarchical Equal Risk Contribution (HERC)
docs.text:
HERC extends HRP by replacing the inverse-variance cluster weights at each bisection step with equal risk contribution weights within each cluster. This enforces risk parity not just at the asset level but at every level of the hierarchy.

At each cluster node, the intra-cluster weights are the ERC solution:

\[ \min_{y_C \geq 0} \; \frac{1}{2} y_C^\top \Sigma_C y_C - \sum_{i \in C} \ln y_{C,i} \]

The inter-cluster allocation still follows the same recursive bisection as HRP, but using the ERC cluster variance instead of the IVP cluster variance.

docs.title: Nested Cluster Optimization (NCO)
docs.text: López de Prado (2019). NCO applies two-level Markowitz optimization:

docs.title: Step 1: Cluster Detection
docs.text: Apply k-means clustering to the correlation matrix (using the first \(k\) principal components as cluster features) to partition assets into \(K\) clusters.

docs.title: Step 2: Intra-Cluster Optimization
docs.text:
Run a within-cluster Markowitz optimization for each cluster \(C_k\) independently:

\[ w^{intra}_{C_k} = \arg\min_{w \geq 0} w^\top \Sigma_{C_k} w \]

This produces one synthetic "cluster portfolio" per cluster.

docs.title: Step 3: Inter-Cluster Optimization
docs.text:
Build a reduced \(K \times K\) covariance matrix from the cluster portfolio returns, and run a second Markowitz optimization across cluster representatives:

\[ w^{inter} = \arg\min_{u \geq 0} u^\top \Sigma^{cluster} u \]

docs.title: Step 4: Combine
docs.text:
The final weight for asset \(i\) in cluster \(C_k\) is:

\[ w_i = w^{intra}_{i \in C_k} \times w^{inter}_{C_k} \]

docs.title: Comparison
docs.text: Property HRP HERC NCO Matrix inversion ❌ ❌ ✅ (within clusters only) Risk budget control Implicit (IVP) Explicit (ERC) Implicit (MinVol) Cluster method Hierarchical linkage Hierarchical linkage K-Means Complexity Low Medium Higher Large universe (100+) ✅ ✅ ✅

docs.title: 4. Spectral Graph Laplacian HRP (SpectralLaplacianHRPAllocator)
docs.text:
Instead of single-linkage agglomerative clustering on pairwise correlation distances (which is vulnerable to "chaining" noise), SpectralLaplacianHRPAllocator constructs a non-negative precision/partial-correlation adjacency matrix \(W_S\) on each induced subgraph \(S \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}\) and computes the normalized Graph Laplacian:

\[ \mathcal{L}_S = I_{|S|} - D_S^{-1/2} W_S D_S^{-1/2} \]

The second smallest eigenvector \(v_2(\mathcal{L}_S)\) (Fiedler vector) provides a 1D spectral embedding along which a Cheeger sweep cut partitions \(S \to (S_L, S_R)\) to minimize normalized cut conductance. During recursive bisection, cluster variances are penalized by internal algebraic connectivity \(\lambda_2(\mathcal{L}_{S})\):

\[ \tilde{V}(S_c) = V_{\text{IVP}}(S_c) \cdot \left(1 + \eta_{\text{frag}} \, \lambda_2(\mathcal{L}_{S_c})\right), \qquad \alpha_L = 1 - \frac{\tilde{V}(S_L)}{\tilde{V}(S_L) + \tilde{V}(S_R)} \]

docs.text:

  • Raffinot (2018) — Hierarchical Clustering-Based Asset Allocation

docs.title: Monte Carlo & Entropy Pooling Mathematics
docs.text: This page covers the mathematical foundations of the scenario generators, missing-history imputation, Meucci's Entropy Pooling (first- and second-moment views), and path-dependent risk metrics implemented in pyalloq-simulation.

docs.title: 1. PCA Factor Back-Casting Imputation
docs.text:
When asset \(j\) has missing historical observations (e.g., a recent IPO missing \(t \in \mathcal{M}_j\) and observed on \(t \in \mathcal{O}_j\)), FactorBackcastImputer avoids truncating the \(N\)-asset matrix:

  1. Identify anchor assets \(\mathcal{A}\) with coverage \(\ge c_{\min}\) and extract \(K\) orthogonal latent factor series \(F \in \mathbb{R}^{T \times K}\) via Principal Component Analysis on anchor returns.
  2. Estimate ridge-stabilized factor loadings for asset \(j\) on its observed window \(\mathcal{O}_j\):
\[ \hat{\beta}_j = \left(X_{\mathcal{O}_j}^\top X_{\mathcal{O}_j} + \lambda I\right)^{-1} X_{\mathcal{O}_j}^\top r_{j, \mathcal{O}_j}, \quad X_t = [1, F_t] \]
  1. Impute missing returns for \(t \in \mathcal{M}_j\) with matched idiosyncratic residual variance \(\hat{\sigma}_{\epsilon, j}^2\):
\[ \hat{r}_{j, t} = X_t \hat{\beta}_j + \epsilon_{j, t}, \quad \epsilon_{j, t} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \hat{\sigma}_{\epsilon, j}^2) \]
  1. Back-cast pre-IPO prices recursively from the first observed price \(P_{j, t_0}\):
\[ P_{j, t} = \frac{P_{j, t+1}}{1 + \hat{r}_{j, t+1}}, \quad t = t_0 - 1, \dots, 0 \]

docs.title: Filtered Historical Simulation (FHSGenerator)
docs.text:
Filtered Historical Simulation (Barone-Adesi et al., 1999) strips volatility clustering using univariate GARCH(1,1) models while preserving empirical cross-asset dependence and fat tails via non-parametric residual bootstrapping:

\[ r_{i, t} = \mu_i + \epsilon_{i, t}, \quad \epsilon_{i, t} = \sigma_{i, t} z_{i, t} \] \[ \sigma_{i, t}^2 = \omega_i + \alpha_i \epsilon_{i, t-1}^2 + \beta_i \sigma_{i, t-1}^2 \]

At each simulated step \(t\), a random historical date index \(\tau \sim \text{Uniform}\{1, \dots, T_{\text{hist}}\}\) is drawn synchronously across all \(N\) assets, preserving cross-sectional co-movement \(Z_{\tau} = (\hat{z}_{1, \tau}, \dots, \hat{z}_{N, \tau})\).

docs.title: GARCH-EVT-Student-\(t\) Copula (GARCHEVTCopulaGenerator)
docs.text:
To model extreme tail risk and positive lower-tail dependence (\(\lambda_L > 0\)), GARCHEVTCopulaGenerator combines AR(1)-GARCH(1,1) filtration with Extreme Value Theory (McNeil & Frey, 2000) and a Student-\(t\) Copula:

  1. AR(1)-GARCH(1,1) Filtration: Extracts standardized residuals \(z_{i, t} = \epsilon_{i, t} / \sigma_{i, t}\).
  2. Semi-Parametric Generalized Pareto (GPD) Marginals: Given lower and upper quantile thresholds \(u_L, u_U\) at probabilities \(q_L, q_U\), exceedances in the tails follow the Generalized Pareto Distribution:
\[ F_i(z) = egin{cases} q_L \left(1 - G_{\xi_{L,i}, eta_{L,i}}(u_L - z) ight) & z < u_L \ \hat{F}_{ ext{emp}}(z) & u_L \le z \le u_U \ q_U + (1 - q_U) G_{\xi_{U,i}, eta_{U,i}}(z - u_U) & z > u_U \end{cases} \]

where the GPD cumulative distribution function is:

\[ G_{\xi, eta}(y) = 1 - \left(1 + rac{\xi y}{ eta} ight)^{-1/\xi} \]
  1. Student-\(t\) Copula Binding: Uniform marginals \(u_{i, t} = F_i(z_{i, t})\) are mapped via the univariate Student-\(t\) quantile \(t_ u^{-1}(u_{i, t})\) to estimate the copula correlation matrix \(R\) with degrees of freedom \( u\). Lower-tail dependence between assets \(i\) and \(j\) is strictly positive:
\[ \lambda_L = 2 \, t_{ u + 1}\!\left(-\sqrt{ rac{( u + 1)(1 - ho_{ij})}{1 + ho_{ij}}} ight) > 0 \]

docs.title: Gaussian Mixture Markov Regimes (GMMRegimeGenerator)
docs.text:
Models discrete latent market states \(s_t \in \{1, \dots, K\}\) via a \(K\)-component Gaussian Mixture Model:

\[ p(r_t) = \sum_{k=1}^K \pi_k \, \mathcal{N}(r_t \mid \mu_k, \Sigma_k) \]

Historical states are decoded via maximum a posteriori assignment \(\hat{s}_t = \arg\max_k \gamma_{t, k}\), yielding the empirical Markov transition matrix \(P \in \mathbb{R}^{K \times K}\) with entries \(P_{ab} = \mathbb{P}(s_{t} = b \mid s_{t-1} = a)\). Forward paths evolve \(s_{m, t} \sim P_{s_{m, t-1}, \cdot}\) and draw \(r_{m, t} \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_{s_{m, t}}, \Sigma_{s_{m, t}})\).

docs.title: Stochastic Graph Reaction-Diffusion Contagion (ReactionDiffusionGenerator)
docs.text:
To simulate multi-period network contagion and endogenous volatility spillover across \(M\) paths and \(T\) steps into a 3D ScenarioMarketData tensor \((M, T, N)\), ReactionDiffusionGenerator couples the FitzHugh-Nagumo Graph Reaction-Diffusion PDE on the precision Graph Laplacian \(\mathcal{L}\) with correlated return innovations and the asymmetric leverage effect \(\operatorname{Corr}(dB_{m,t}^{(r)}, dB_{m,t}^{(v)}) = \rho_{\text{lev}} \le 0\):

\[ dv_{m,t} = \left[ -D_v \mathcal{L} v_{m,t} - \kappa_v v_{m,t} + \gamma_{\text{react}} v_{m,t}(v_{m,t} - \theta_{\text{crit}})(1 - v_{m,t}) - \beta_u u_{m,t} \right] dt + \eta_v \, dB_{m,t}^{(v)} \] \[ du_{m,t} = \left[ -D_u \mathcal{L} u_{m,t} + \epsilon_u (v_{m,t} - 0.8 u_{m,t}) \right] dt \] \[ r_{m,t} = \mu + \left(\bar{\sigma} \odot \exp(v_{m,t})\right) \odot dB_{m,t}^{(r)}, \qquad dB_{m,t}^{(r)} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \Gamma_0) \]

When a negative return shock hits asset \(i\), the negative leverage correlation \(\rho_{\text{lev}} < 0\) excites \(v_{m,t,i}\), which then diffuses via \(-D_v \mathcal{L} v_{m,t}\) across connected neighbors in the precision network.

docs.title: Factor-Based Conditional Diffusion (ConditionalDiffusionGenerator)
docs.text:
To synthesize non-parametric cross-sectional trajectories without suffering from the \(N \gg T\) curse of dimensionality, ConditionalDiffusionGenerator projects standardized returns \(Z_t = (R_t - \mu) \oslash \sigma \in \mathbb{R}^N\) onto \(K = \min(K_{\max}, N)\) orthogonal SVD factor loadings \(V_K \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times K}\):

\[ F_t = Z_t V_K \in \mathbb{R}^K, \qquad E_t = Z_t - F_t V_K^\top \in \mathbb{R}^N \]

Under a cosine variance schedule \(\bar{\alpha}_\tau \in (0, 1)\) (Nichol & Dhariwal, 2021), forward diffusion corrupts factor vectors via \(x_\tau = \sqrt{\bar{\alpha}_\tau} F_t + \sqrt{1 - \bar{\alpha}_\tau} \varepsilon\) (\(\varepsilon \sim \mathcal{N}(0, I_K)\)). A conditional score network \(\hat{\varepsilon}_\theta(x_\tau, \tau, c_{t-1})\) is calibrated conditioned on: 1. Trailing factor mean and volatility over condition_window, 2. Point-in-Time implied_vol ratio and cross-sectional dispersion, 3. Depth-2 Rough Log-Signature invariants \((\Delta F, \mathcal{A}_{\text{Lévy}})\).

Forward paths are generated via accelerated DDIM reverse sampling across a subsequence \(\tau_S > \tau_{S-1} > \dots > 0\):

\[ \hat{x}_0 = \frac{x_\tau - \sqrt{1 - \bar{\alpha}_\tau}\,\hat{\varepsilon}_\theta(x_\tau, \tau, c_t)}{\sqrt{\bar{\alpha}_\tau}}, \qquad x_{\tau_{\text{prev}}} = \sqrt{\bar{\alpha}_{\tau_{\text{prev}}}} \hat{x}_0 + \sqrt{1 - \bar{\alpha}_{\tau_{\text{prev}}} - \sigma_\tau^2}\,\hat{\varepsilon}_\theta + \sigma_\tau z \]

and recombined with kurtosis-matched Student-\(t\) idiosyncratic innovations \(E_{m,t}\).

docs.title: Arbitrage-Free Coupled Jump-Diffusion Neural SDE (NeuralSDEGenerator & NeuralSDEEstimator)
docs.text:
NeuralSDEGenerator and NeuralSDEEstimator parameterize continuous-time price-volatility jump-diffusion dynamics over \(t \in [0, H]\):

\[ dX_t = \mu_\theta^{\text{arb-free}}(t, X_t, V_t)\,dt + D(V_t) L_{\text{corr}}\,dW_t^{(X)} + \left(J_t\,dN_t(\lambda) - \lambda \bar{\mu}_J\,dt\right) \] \[ dV_t = \left(-\kappa V_t + g_\theta(X_t, V_t)\right) dt + \xi\,dW_t^{(V)}, \qquad D(V_t) = \operatorname{diag}\!\left(\bar{\sigma} \odot \exp(0.5 V_t)\right) \]
  1. Hansen-Jagannathan Market-Price-of-Risk Bound (No-Statistical-Arbitrage): At every step, the instantaneous Sharpe vector \(\theta_t = L_{\text{corr}}^{-1} D(V_t)^{-1}(\mu_\theta - r_f \mathbf{1})\) is radially projected onto the ball of radius \(\theta_{\max, \Delta t} = \theta_{\max} / \sqrt{252}\):
\[ \tilde{\theta}_t = \theta_t \cdot \min\!\left(1, \frac{\theta_{\max, \Delta t}}{\|\theta_t\|_2}\right), \qquad \mu_\theta^{\text{arb-free}} = r_f \mathbf{1} + D(V_t) L_{\text{corr}} \tilde{\theta}_t \]
  1. Depth-2 Rough Log-Signature MMD Calibration: In addition to Cholesky transition negative log-likelihood, NeuralSDEEstimator minimizes the discrepancy between empirical and simulated windowed Depth-2 Lyndon log-signatures:
\[ \mathcal{L}_{\text{Sig-MMD}}^2 = \left\| \mathbb{E}_{X \sim \mathbb{P}_{\text{emp}}}\!\left[\operatorname{LogSig}_2(X)\right] - \mathbb{E}_{\hat{X} \sim \mathbb{P}_\theta}\!\left[\operatorname{LogSig}_2(\hat{X})\right] \right\|_2^2 \]

docs.title: 3. Meucci's Entropy Pooling (EntropyPooler & ViewBuilder)
docs.text:
Given \(M\) simulated scenarios with prior probability vector \(p \in \Delta^M\) (typically uniform \(p_m = 1/M\)), Entropy Pooling (Meucci, 2008) finds the posterior probability distribution \(x \in \Delta^M\) that satisfies linear equality and inequality views while minimizing Relative Entropy (Kullback-Leibler divergence):

\[ \min_{x \in \mathbb{R}^M} \mathcal{E}(x \,\|\, p) = \sum_{m=1}^{M} x_m \ln\!\left(\frac{x_m}{p_m}\right) \]

subject to:

\[ A x \le b, \quad C x = d, \quad \mathbf{1}^\top x = 1, \quad x \ge 0 \]

docs.title: Unconstrained Dual Formulation
docs.text:
Rather than solving an \(M\)-dimensional primal problem (\(M \sim 10,000\)), EntropyPooler solves the low-dimensional Lagrange dual over the \(V\) view multipliers \(\gamma = (\lambda, u)\) where \( u \ge 0\):

\[ \min_{\lambda, u \ge 0} \; \ln\!\left(\sum_{m=1}^M p_m \exp\!\left(-[G^ op \gamma]_m ight) ight) + \gamma^ op ext{targets}, \quad G = egin{bmatrix} C \ A \end{bmatrix} \]

The posterior scenario weights are recovered analytically via the log-sum-exp stabilized Boltzmann-Gibbs distribution:

\[ x^*_m = rac{p_m \exp\!\left(-[G^ op \gamma^*]_m ight)}{\sum_{k=1}^M p_k \exp\!\left(-[G^ op \gamma^*]_k ight)} \]

docs.title: First- and Second-Moment View Linearization
docs.text:
Because expectation under the scenario measure is a linear inner product \(\mathbb{E}_x[g(R)] = \sum_{m=1}^M x_m g(R_m)\), both first- and second-moment views are linear in the probability vector \(x\):

Absolute Return View (AbsoluteView):

\[ \sum_{m=1}^M x_m R_{m, i} \;\in\; \{\le, =, \ge\}\; \mu_i^{\text{target}} \]

Relative Return View (RelativeView):

\[ \sum_{m=1}^M x_m (R_{m, i} - R_{m, j}) \;\in\; \{\le, =, \ge\}\; \delta_{ij}^{\text{target}} \]

Volatility View (VolatilityView) — centered around the reference mean \(\bar{\mu}_i\):

\[ \sum_{m=1}^M x_m (R_{m, i} - \bar{\mu}_i)^2 \;\in\; \{\le, =, \ge\}\; \left(\sigma_i^{\text{target}}\right)^2 \]

Covariance / Correlation View (CovarianceView):

\[ \sum_{m=1}^M x_m (R_{m, i} - \bar{\mu}_i)(R_{m, j} - \bar{\mu}_j) \;\in\; \{\le, =, \ge\}\; \rho_{ij}^{\text{target}} \bar{\sigma}_i \bar{\sigma}_j \]

docs.title: 4. Path-Dependent Risk Metrics (ScenarioEvaluator)
docs.text:
Let \(W_{m, t}\) denote the simulated portfolio wealth on path \(m \in \{1, \dots, M\}\) at time step \(t \in \{0, \dots, T\}\) with \(W_{m, 0} = 1\):

Path Maximum Drawdown (\(\text{MDD}_m\)):

\[ \text{MDD}_m = \min_{0 \le t \le T} \frac{W_{m, t} - \max_{0 \le \tau \le t} W_{m, \tau}}{\max_{0 \le \tau \le t} W_{m, \tau}} \le 0 \]

View-Adjusted Maximum Drawdown:

\[ \text{MDD}_{\text{view}} = \sum_{m=1}^M x^*_m \, \text{MDD}_m \]

Probability of Ruin (\(\mathbb{P}_{\text{ruin}}\)) — for critical drawdown threshold \(\theta_{\text{ruin}} < 0\) (e.g., \(-0.30\)):

\[ \mathbb{P}_{\text{ruin}}(\theta_{\text{ruin}}) = \sum_{m=1}^M x^*_m \, \mathbb{I}\!\left(\text{MDD}_m \le \theta_{\text{ruin}}\right) \]

docs.title: Combinatorial Symmetric Cross-Validation (PBOEvaluator)
docs.text:
Given a return matrix \(M_{\text{trials}} \in \mathbb{R}^{T \times M}\) of \(M\) candidate strategy configurations evaluated over \(T\) observations, CSCV (Bailey et al., 2017) partitions time into \(S\) even submatrices and forms all \(C = \binom{S}{S/2}\) training (In-Sample, \(J\)) and testing (Out-of-Sample, \(\bar{J}\)) combinations:

  1. For each split \(c \in \{1, \dots, C\}\), compute the vector of In-Sample Sharpe ratios \(R_c \in \mathbb{R}^M\) on \(J_c\) and Out-of-Sample Sharpe ratios \(\bar{R}_c \in \mathbb{R}^M\) on \(\bar{J}_c\).
  2. Select the In-Sample optimal strategy \(m^* = \arg\max_m R_{c, m}\) and find its relative rank \(\omega_c \in (0, 1)\) within the Out-of-Sample distribution \(\bar{R}_c\).
  3. Define the Rank Logit \(\lambda_c\):
\[ \lambda_c = \ln\!\left(\frac{\omega_c}{1 - \omega_c}\right) \]

When \(\lambda_c \le 0\), the strategy selected as best In-Sample performs worse than the median strategy Out-of-Sample. The Probability of Backtest Overfitting (PBO) is the empirical probability mass in the left tail:

\[ \text{PBO} = \frac{1}{C} \sum_{c=1}^C \mathbb{I}\!\left(\lambda_c \le 0\right) \]

docs.title: Combinatorial Purged Cross-Validation (CPCVSplitter)
docs.text: Given \(N\) chronological groups and \(k\) test groups per split, there are \(\binom{N}{k}\) train/test splits with purge window \(p\) and embargo window \(e\) applied around every test block boundary. Because each group appears in exactly \(\varphi(N, k) = \binom{N - 1}{k - 1}\) test sets across all splits, the out-of-sample predictions can be reassembled into \(\varphi(N, k)\) full-horizon backtest paths rather than a single point estimate (López de Prado, 2018).

docs.title: Multi-Period Portfolio Optimization (MPO) — Mathematical Foundations
docs.text:
Single-period portfolio optimization (SPO) treats each rebalance date \(t\) as an isolated static problem, ignoring the intertemporal coupling induced by transaction costs, nonlinear market impact, multi-horizon alpha decay, and future rebalancing flexibility.

PyAlloq implements a unified 3-Pillar Multi-Period Portfolio Optimization (MPO) framework bridging:

  1. Classical Convex Model Predictive Control (MPC) & Operator Splitting (ADMM) (Boyd et al., 2017; Gârleanu & Pedersen, 2013)
  2. Decision-Focused Deep Learning (DFL) & Entropic Mirror-Descent Fixed-Point (MDFP) Layers (Agrawal et al., 2019; Elmachtoub & Grigas, 2022)
  3. FinRL Deep Reinforcement Learning, Two-Level Bayesian HRP (RL-BHRP), Deep Hedging Trajectory Optimization, & Thermodynamic Regime Gating (Buehler et al., 2019; Liu et al., 2022; Moroke et al., 2026)

docs.title: 1. Intertemporal Wealth & Self-Financing Dynamics
docs.text:
Let \(N\) risky assets (plus an optional cash account) have gross simple return vector \(R_{t+1} = \mathbf{1} + r_{t+1} \in \mathbb{R}_{++}^N\) over period \([t, t+1]\).

At the beginning of period \(t\):

  • \(w_{t^-} \in \Delta^N\) denotes the pre-trade drifted weight vector inherited from period \(t-1\).
  • \(z_t \in \mathbb{R}^N\) denotes the normalized trade vector executed at time \(t\), resulting in the post-trade weight vector: [ w_t = w_{t^-} + z_t, \qquad \mathbf{1}^\top z_t + \phi_{\text{trade}}(z_t) = 0 \quad (\text{or } \mathbf{1}^\top w_t = 1 \text{ under self-financing rescale}). ]
  • Over period \([t, t+1]\), market returns cause the post-trade weights \(w_t\) to drift nonlinearly to the next pre-trade state \(w_{(t+1)^-}\): [ w_{(t+1)^-} = \frac{w_t \circ (\mathbf{1} + r_{t+1})}{1 + r_{p, t+1}^{\text{net}}}, \qquad r_{p, t+1}^{\text{net}} = (1 - \phi_{\text{trade}}(z_t))(1 + w_t^\top r_{t+1}) - 1. ]

Within a convex lookahead planning horizon \(\tau = t, \dots, t+H-1\) where future returns are small (\(\|r_\tau\|_\infty \ll 1\)), the linearized intertemporal state transition holds: [ w_\tau = w_{\tau-1} + z_\tau, \qquad w_{t-1} \equiv w_{t^-}. ]

docs.title: 2. Microstructural Transaction Cost & Market Impact Models
docs.text:
At each planning stage \(\tau\), rebalancing trades \(z_\tau = w_\tau - w_{\tau-1}\) incur temporary and permanent execution costs:

\[ \phi_{\text{trade}}(z_\tau) = \underbrace{\left(\kappa_{\text{spread}}^\top |z_\tau|\right)}_{\text{Proportional Bid-Ask } (p=1)} + \underbrace{\left(\kappa_{\text{impact}}^\top |z_\tau|^{3/2}\right)}_{\text{Square-Root Market Impact } (p=3/2)} + \underbrace{\frac{1}{2} z_\tau^\top \Lambda_\tau z_\tau}_{\text{Quadratic Temporary Cost } (p=2)}. \]

docs.title: 2.1 Proportional Bid-Ask Spread (\(p=1\)) & the No-Trade Zone
docs.text: The \(\ell_1\) penalty \(\kappa_{\text{spread}}^\top |w_\tau - w_{\tau-1}|\) is non-differentiable at \(z_{\tau,i} = 0\). By first-order subdifferential KKT conditions: [ \hat{\mu}{\tau,i} - \gamma (\Sigma\tau w_\tau)i - \nu\tau \in [-\kappa_{\text{spread},i}, +\kappa_{\text{spread},i}] \implies z_{\tau,i}^ = 0. ] Thus, proportional costs create a rigorous polyhedral no-trade region* around \(w_{t^-}\): the optimizer holds existing positions untouched unless the marginal risk-adjusted alpha exceeds the half-spread threshold \(\kappa_{\text{spread},i}\).

docs.title: 2.2 Square-Root Market Impact (\(p=3/2\)) via Power Cones
docs.text: Following Almgren & Chriss (2001) and Boyd et al. (2017), executing a fraction of Average Daily Volume (ADV) incurs price impact proportional to \(|z_{\tau,i}|^{1/2}\), yielding total dollar cost proportional to \(|z_{\tau,i}|^{3/2}\): [ \kappa_{\text{impact},i} |z_{\tau,i}|^{3/2}, \qquad \kappa_{\text{impact},i} \propto \sigma_i \sqrt{\frac{V_{\text{port}}}{\text{ADV}_i}}. ] In CVXPY, cp.power(cp.abs(z_tau), 1.5) is canonicalized into 3D power cones / second-order cones (SOCP) solvable in polynomial interior-point iterations.

docs.title: 2.3 Gârleanu-Pedersen (2013) Permanent Price Impact & Aim Portfolios
docs.text: When large institutional trades move the equilibrium market price permanently, an intertemporal price-distortion state \(q_\tau \in \mathbb{R}^N\) evolves with resilience rate \(\rho_{\text{perm}} \in (0, 1]\): [ q_\tau = (1 - \rho_{\text{perm}}) q_{\tau-1} + \eta_{\text{perm}} z_\tau, \qquad q_{t-1} = \mathbf{0}, ] imposing an additional stage execution drag \(\frac{1}{2} q_\tau^\top q_\tau\). Under quadratic costs and exponential alpha decay, Gârleanu & Pedersen (2013) prove that the optimal multi-period policy trades partially at constant speed toward an Aim Portfolio \(w_t^{\text{aim}}\), which itself is a discounted convex combination of future single-period Markowitz portfolios.

docs.title: 3. Multi-Horizon Alpha Decay & Term Structure
docs.text:
Alpha signals decay at heterogeneous rates across horizons \(h = 1, \dots, H\). Let \(K\) signal families (e.g., short-term reversal, medium-term momentum, slow value/carry) have half-lives \(H_{1/2}^{(k)}\) and decay rates \(\lambda_k = \frac{\ln 2}{H_{1/2}^{(k)}}\).

The expected return forecast at horizon step \(h \in \{0, \dots, H-1\}\) is: [ \hat{\mu}{t+h|t} = \sum. ] Implemented in }^K \exp(-\lambda_k h) \, s_{t}^{(k)AlphaDecayReturnEstimator, this prevents fast-decaying signals from triggering high-turnover trades that cannot amortize round-trip execution costs.

docs.title: 4. Pillar 1: Classical Convex MPC & ADMM Operator Splitting
4.1 Deterministic Receding-Horizon MPC Formulation
docs.text:
At each rebalance date \(t\), MultiPeriodMPCAllocator solves the \(H\)-stage convex optimization problem:

\[ \begin{aligned} \max_{\{w_\tau, z_\tau\}_{\tau=t}^{t+H-1}} \quad & \sum_{\tau=t}^{t+H-1} \beta^{\tau-t} \left[ \hat{\mu}_{\tau|t}^\top w_\tau - \frac{\gamma}{2} w_\tau^\top \hat{\Sigma}_{\tau|t} w_\tau - \phi_{\text{trade}}(z_\tau) - \phi_{\text{hold}}(w_\tau) \right] - \frac{\gamma_{\text{term}}}{2} (w_{t+H-1} - w_{\text{bench}})^\top \hat{\Sigma}_{t+H-1|t} (w_{t+H-1} - w_{\text{bench}}) \\ \text{subject to} \quad & w_\tau = w_{\tau-1} + z_\tau, \qquad w_{t-1} = w_{t^-}, \\ & \mathbf{1}^\top w_\tau = 1, \qquad w_{\min} \le w_\tau \le w_{\max}, \\ & \|z_\tau\|_1 \le \tau_{\max} \quad \forall \tau \in \{t, \dots, t+H-1\}. \end{aligned} \]

By the Receding-Horizon Principle, only the immediate stage decision \(w_t^*\) is executed in the market; at \(t+1\), the horizon rolls forward with updated pre-trade weights \(w_{(t+1)^-}\).

docs.title: 4.2 High-Speed Operator Splitting via ADMM
docs.text:
For large universes or high-frequency backtests where interior-point solvers become a bottleneck, MultiPeriodMPCAllocator(backend="admm") reformulates the coupled \(H\)-stage problem using Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM):

  1. Primal Weight & Trade Variable Split: Introduce auxiliary split variables \(u_\tau = z_\tau = w_\tau - w_{\tau-1}\) and \(v_\tau = w_\tau\) with scaled dual variables \(\eta_\tau, \xi_\tau\).
  2. Block-Tridiagonal KKT Linear System (\(w\)-update): Solving for the stacked trajectory \(W = (w_t, \dots, w_{t+H-1})\) reduces to a positive-definite block-tridiagonal linear system inverted via block Thomas elimination.
  3. Closed-Form Proximal Soft-Thresholding (\(u\)-update): The non-smooth \(\ell_1\) bid-ask cost and turnover ball decouple into elementwise soft-thresholding: [ \mathcal{S}_{\kappa / \rho}(x) = \operatorname{sign}(x) \max(|x| - \kappa/\rho, \, 0), ] followed by Euclidean projection onto the \(\ell_1\)-turnover ball.
  4. Capped Simplex Projection (\(v\)-update): Projects each \(v_\tau\) onto \(\{w \in \mathbb{R}^N : \mathbf{1}^\top w = 1, \, w_{\min} \le w \le w_{\max}\}\) in \(O(N \log N)\) time.

docs.title: 4.3 Scenario-Tree Stochastic MPC with CVaR Tail Control
docs.text: When ScenarioMarketData provides \(M\) Monte Carlo paths \(R^{(m)} \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times N}\) with probabilities \(p_m\) (e.g., from GARCHEVTCopulaGenerator or EntropyPooler), StochasticScenarioMPCAllocator enforces non-anticipativity at \(t=0\) and optimizes expected multi-stage return minus Rockafellar-Uryasev Conditional Value-at-Risk (\(\text{CVaR}_\alpha\)) of cumulative path loss \(L_m\): [ \text{CVaR}\alpha(L) = \min^M p_m u_m \;\middle|\; u_m \ge L_m - \zeta \right}. ]}, \, u_m \ge 0} \left{ \zeta + \frac{1}{1 - \alpha} \sum_{m=1

docs.title: 5. Pillar 2: Decision-Focused Learning (DFL) & Differentiable MDFP Layers
5.1 The Objective Mismatch of Two-Stage "Predict-Then-Optimize"
docs.text:
Training a neural network exclusively on Mean Squared Error \(\mathcal{L}_{\text{MSE}}(\hat{\mu}, y) = \|\hat{\mu} - y\|_2^2\) treats all return forecast errors equally. However, inside a constrained multi-period optimizer:

  • Errors on assets deep inside the no-trade zone have zero impact on portfolio weights.
  • Small sign errors on assets near the simplex boundary or with low covariance can trigger massive, costly turnover cascades across stages \(t, \dots, t+H-1\).

docs.title: 5.2 Entropic Mirror-Descent Fixed-Point (MDFP) Optimization Layer
docs.text:
To embed multi-period optimization directly inside PyTorch computation graphs without expensive CPU-bound conic solvers, MDFPOptimizationLayer solves the coupled \(H\)-stage simplex problem using Entropic Mirror Descent (Exponentiated Gradient) under the Kullback-Leibler Bregman divergence \(D_{\text{KL}}(z \| z')\):

[ z_{s,i}^{(m+1)} = \frac{z_{s,i}^{(m)} \exp!\left(-\eta \, g_{s,i}^{(m)}\right)}{\sum_{j=1}^N z_{s,j}^{(m)} \exp!\left(-\eta \, g_{s,j}^{(m)}\right)} \equiv \mathcal{F}_{s,i}!\left(z^{(m)}, \theta\right), ] where \(g_s^{(m)} = \nabla_{z_s} J(z^{(m)}; \theta)\) is the stage gradient incorporating expected returns, covariance risk \(\gamma \Sigma_s z_s\), and smoothed inter-stage turnover coupling \(\kappa \frac{z_s - z_{s-1}}{\sqrt{(z_s - z_{s-1})^2 + \epsilon^2}}\).

docs.title: 5.3 \(O(1)\)-Memory Implicit Fixed-Point Differentiation
docs.text: Rather than unrolling \(M\) mirror-descent steps in autograd memory, MDFPOptimizationLayer differentiates through the converged fixed point \(z^* = \mathcal{F}(z^*, \theta)\) via the Implicit Function Theorem: [ z^(\theta) = \mathcal{F}(z^(\theta), \theta) \implies \left(I - \frac{\partial \mathcal{F}}{\partial z^}\right) \frac{\partial z^}{\partial \theta} = \frac{\partial \mathcal{F}}{\partial \theta}. ] In the backward pass, given upstream gradient \(v = \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial z^*}\), we solve the adjoint linear system via a damped Neumann Series of Vector-Jacobian Products (VJPs) evaluated exclusively at \(z^*\): [ u^\top = v^\top \left(I - \lambda \frac{\partial \mathcal{F}}{\partial z^}\right)^{-1} = \sum_{k=0}^K v^\top \left(\lambda \frac{\partial \mathcal{F}}{\partial z^}\right)^k, \qquad \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial \theta} = u^\top \frac{\partial \mathcal{F}(z^*, \theta)}{\partial \theta}. ]

docs.title: 5.4 SPO+ Surrogate & Hybrid DFL Losses
docs.text:
PyAlloq provides two decision-focused training objectives in dfl.py:

  1. Multi-Period SPO+ Convex Surrogate Loss (SPOPlusLoss): [ \mathcal{L}_{\text{SPO}+}(\hat{\mu}, y) = J!\left(z^(2\hat{\mu} - y); \, 2\hat{\mu} - y\right) + 2 \langle \hat{\mu}, \, z^(y) - z^(2\hat{\mu} - y) \rangle - J(z^(y); y). ]
  2. Hybrid Decision-Focused Loss (HybridDFLLoss): [ \mathcal{L}{\text{Hybrid}} = \alpha \, \mathcal{L} - y|_2^2, \qquad \alpha \in [0, 1], ] combining multi-period net-of-cost decision utility with MSE regularization to stabilize representation learning in low-SNR financial regimes.}}!\left(z^*(\hat{\mu}), y\right) + (1 - \alpha) \, |\hat{\mu

docs.title: 6. Pillar 3: FinRL DRL, RL-BHRP, Deep Hedging & Thermodynamic Gates
6.1 FinRL Markov Decision Process (MDP) & Turbulence Circuit Breaker
docs.text:
In PortfolioGymEnv, multi-period portfolio management is cast as a continuous-control MDP \((\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{A}, \mathcal{P}, \mathcal{R}, \gamma)\):

  • State \(s_t\): Concatenation of pre-trade drifted weights \(w_{t^-}\), lookback return tensor \(R_{t-L+1:t}\), rolling volatilities \(\sigma_t\), Mahalanobis Turbulence Index \(d_t\), and Bures-Wasserstein regime distance \(W_2\): [ d_t = \frac{1}{N} (r_t - \hat{\mu}_t)^\top \hat{\Sigma}_t^{-1} (r_t - \hat{\mu}_t). ]
  • Reward \(r_t\): Differential log net wealth growth penalized by quadratic return variance and thermodynamic turnover friction: [ r_t = \ln(1 + r_{p,t}^{\text{net}}) - \frac{\gamma}{2} (r_{p,t}^{\text{net}})^2 - \eta_{W_2} W_2(t) |w_t - w_{t^-}|_1. ]

docs.title: 6.2 Two-Level Bayesian Hierarchical Risk Parity (RL-BHRP)
docs.text:
BayesianHRPAllocator resolves the return-insensitivity of classical HRP without inverting ill-conditioned \(N \times N\) covariance matrices:

  1. Intra-Cluster Level: Hierarchical clustering partitions the \(N\) assets into \(K\) correlation clusters, and recursive bisection computes risk-parity intra-cluster weights \(W_{\text{intra}} \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times K}\).
  2. Inter-Cluster Bayesian Level: Cluster-level equilibrium implied returns \(\pi_C = \Sigma_C b_{\text{hrp}}\) are blended with sample/predicted cluster views \(\mu_C^{\text{view}}\): [ \bar{\mu}_C = (1 - \tau) \pi_C + \tau \mu_C^{\text{view}}, ] and cluster budgets are tilted toward high-posterior-Sharpe clusters while damping cluster turnover against \(w_{t^-}\).

docs.title: 6.3 Deep Hedging Pathwise Trajectory Optimization
docs.text: Rather than relying on noisy TD(0) Bellman bootstrapping, DeepHedgingTrajectoryTrainer unrolls TrajectoryPolicyNet \(\pi_\theta(R_{t-L+1:t}, w_{t^-})\) along \(H\)-step sample paths \(\omega_j\) and minimizes the Entropic Risk Measure of cumulative net wealth via direct pathwise backpropagation: [ \mathcal{L}{\text{DH}}(\theta) = \frac{1}{\gamma} \ln \left( \frac{1}{M} \sum(\omega_j; \theta) \right) \right). ]}^M \exp!\left( -\gamma \sum_{s=0}^{H-1} r_{p, t+s}^{\text{net}

docs.title: 6.4 Thermodynamic & Bures-Wasserstein Regime Gate (Moroke et al., 2026)
docs.text:
WassersteinRegimeGate models the portfolio rebalancing cycle as a non-equilibrium stochastic heat engine coupled to a fast market bath \(\mathcal{N}(\mu_{\text{fast}}, \Sigma_{\text{fast}})\) at temperature \(T_{\text{fast}} = \frac{1}{N}\operatorname{Tr}(\Sigma_{\text{fast}})\) and a slow structural bath \(\mathcal{N}(\mu_{\text{slow}}, \Sigma_{\text{slow}})\) at temperature \(T_{\text{slow}} = \frac{1}{N}\operatorname{Tr}(\Sigma_{\text{slow}})\):

  1. Bures-Wasserstein 2-Distance: [ W_2^2(\mathcal{N}{\text{fast}}, \mathcal{N}|}}) = |\mu_{\text{fast}} - \mu_{\text{slow}2^2 + \operatorname{Tr}!\left(\Sigma\right). ]}} + \Sigma_{\text{slow}} - 2\left(\Sigma_{\text{fast}}^{1/2} \Sigma_{\text{slow}} \Sigma_{\text{fast}}^{1/2}\right)^{1/2
  2. Carnot Efficiency Bound: [ \eta_{\text{Carnot}} = 1 - \frac{\min(T_{\text{fast}}, T_{\text{slow}})}{\max(T_{\text{fast}}, T_{\text{slow}})}. ]
  3. Thermodynamic Rebalance Gating: When \(W_2 > W_{2,\text{thresh}}\) indicates a structural regime rupture where turnover dissipation exceeds extractable alpha, trades are exponentially damped toward existing holdings \(w_{t^-}\): [ w_t^{\text{gated}} = \lambda_{\text{gate}}(W_2) \, w_t^{\text{target}} + \big(1 - \lambda_{\text{gate}}(W_2)\big) \, w_{t^-}, \qquad \lambda_{\text{gate}}(W_2) = \exp!\left(-\beta_{\text{sens}} \max(0, W_2 - W_{2,\text{thresh}})\right). ]

docs.title: Portfolio Theory
docs.text: This page documents the mathematical formulations behind each classical allocator implemented in pyalloq.

docs.title: Markowitz Mean-Variance Optimization
docs.text: Markowitz (1952) introduced the canonical portfolio optimization framework: find the weights \(w\) that minimize portfolio variance for a given level of expected return.

docs.title: Minimum Variance
docs.text:
\[ \min_{w} \; w^\top \Sigma w \quad \text{subject to} \quad \mathbf{1}^\top w = 1, \quad w \geq 0 \]

where \(\Sigma \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times N}\) is the covariance matrix of asset returns.

docs.title: Maximum Sharpe Ratio
docs.text:
Directly maximizing the Sharpe ratio is non-convex. Tobin's mutual fund separation theorem allows the problem to be recast as a convex quadratic program via the substitution trick:

Let \(y = \kappa w\) where \(\kappa = \frac{1}{(\mu - r_f \mathbf{1})^\top w}\). Then:

\[ \max_{w} \; \frac{(\mu - r_f \mathbf{1})^\top w}{\sqrt{w^\top \Sigma w}} \;\equiv\; \min_{y} \; y^\top \Sigma y \quad \text{s.t.} \quad (\mu - r_f \mathbf{1})^\top y = 1, \quad y \geq 0 \]

Recover weights: \(w^* = y^* / \mathbf{1}^\top y^*\)

docs.title: Maximum Utility (Mean-Variance)
docs.text:
Maximize the mean-variance utility function with a risk aversion parameter \(\lambda\):

\[ \max_{w} \; \mu^\top w - \lambda \cdot w^\top \Sigma w \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \mathbf{1}^\top w = 1, \quad w \geq 0 \]

The risk_aversion field in MarketData controls \(\lambda\).

docs.title: Equal Risk Contribution (Risk Parity)
docs.text:
Maillard, Roncalli & Teïletche (2010) propose portfolios where every asset contributes the same amount of marginal risk to the portfolio.

The marginal risk contribution of asset \(i\) is:

\[ \text{MRC}_i = \frac{\partial \sigma_p}{\partial w_i} = \frac{(\Sigma w)_i}{\sigma_p} \]

The total risk contribution of asset \(i\) is:

\[ \text{TRC}_i = w_i \cdot \text{MRC}_i = \frac{w_i (\Sigma w)_i}{\sigma_p} \]

ERC requires \(\text{TRC}_i = \text{TRC}_j\) for all \(i, j\). This is achieved by solving the equivalent convex problem:

\[ \min_{y \geq 0} \; \frac{1}{2} y^\top \Sigma y - \sum_{i=1}^{N} \ln y_i \]

Then normalize: \(w_i = y_i / \sum_j y_j\)

docs.title: Risk Budgeting
docs.text:
Generalizes ERC by assigning target risk budgets \(b_i \geq 0\) (with \(\sum b_i = 1\)) to each asset:

\[ \min_{y \geq 0} \; \frac{1}{2} y^\top \Sigma y - \sum_{i=1}^{N} b_i \ln y_i \]

When \(b_i = 1/N\) for all \(i\), this reduces to Risk Parity. Pass budgets via MarketData.features["risk_budgets"].

docs.title: Maximum Diversification
docs.text:
Choueifaty & Coignard (2008) define the Diversification Ratio:

\[ D(w) = \frac{w^\top \sigma}{\sqrt{w^\top \Sigma w}} = \frac{\sum_i w_i \sigma_i}{\sigma_p} \]

where \(\sigma_i = \sqrt{\Sigma_{ii}}\) is the individual asset volatility and \(\sigma_p = \sqrt{w^\top \Sigma w}\) is the portfolio volatility.

The maximum diversification portfolio maximizes \(D(w)\), which is equivalent (via the same substitution trick as Max Sharpe) to:

\[ \min_{y \geq 0} \; y^\top \Sigma y \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \sigma^\top y = 1 \]

Recover weights: \(w^* = y^* / \mathbf{1}^\top y^*\)

docs.title: Conditional Value-at-Risk (Rockafellar & Uryasev, 2000)
docs.text:
For a confidence level \(\beta \in (0, 1)\) (e.g., \(\beta = 0.95\)) and historical return matrix \(R \in \mathbb{R}^{T \times N}\), MeanCVaRAllocator minimizes the portfolio Expected Shortfall using the convex Rockafellar-Uryasev linear programming auxiliary formulation:

\[ \min_{w, \alpha, u \ge 0} \; \alpha + \frac{1}{(1 - \beta) T} \sum_{t=1}^T u_t \quad \text{subject to} \quad u_t \ge -r_t^\top w - \alpha, \quad \mathbf{1}^\top w = 1, \quad l \le w \le b \]

At optimality, \(\alpha^*\) equals the daily Value-at-Risk (\(\text{VaR}_\beta\)) and the objective equals \(\text{CVaR}_\beta(w^*)\).

docs.title: Conditional Drawdown-at-Risk (Chekhlov, Uryasev & Zabarankin, 2005)
docs.text:
Let \(C_t(w) = \sum_{\tau=1}^t r_\tau^\top w\) denote the cumulative uncompounded portfolio return at time \(t\), and let \(M_t = \max_{1 \le \tau \le t} C_\tau(w)\) track the running high-water mark. CDaRAllocator minimizes the tail average of drawdowns \(D_t = M_t - C_t(w)\) at level \(\beta\):

\[ \min_{w, M, d \ge 0, \alpha, u \ge 0} \; \alpha + \frac{1}{(1 - \beta) T} \sum_{t=1}^T u_t \]

subject to linear path-monotonicity constraints \(M_t \ge C_t(w)\), \(M_t \ge M_{t-1}\), \(d_t \ge M_t - C_t(w)\), and \(u_t \ge d_t - \alpha\).

docs.title: Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Optimization (WassersteinDROAllocator)
docs.text:
Let \(\hat{\mathbb{P}} = \sum_{i=1}^M p_i \delta_{r_i}\) denote the empirical (or synthetic scenario) distribution over \(M\) return atoms \(r_i \in \mathbb{R}^N\). To hedge against distributional misspecification and structural regime shifts, WassersteinDROAllocator optimizes against the worst-case measure \(\mathbb{Q}\) inside the Expected-Value-Constrained Wasserstein Ambiguity Set (Esfahani & Kuhn, 2018; Fonseca & Junca, 2021; Li, 2023):

\[ \mathcal{P}_{\varepsilon_t}(G, q) = \left\{ \mathbb{Q} \in \mathcal{M}(\mathbb{R}^N) \;:\; W_p(\mathbb{Q}, \hat{\mathbb{P}}) \le \varepsilon_t, \quad \mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{Q}}[G r] = q \right\} \]

docs.title: 1. Ground Metrics & Dual Norm Regularization
docs.text:
For transport cost \(d(r, \hat{r}) = \|r - \hat{r}\|_{\mathcal{G}}\) and effective exposure vector \(u = w - G^\top \lambda\), Kantorovich duality yields the exact dual norm penalty \(\varepsilon_t \|u\|_{\mathcal{G}^*}\):

  • Mahalanobis ("mahalanobis"): \(d(r, \hat{r}) = \|\Sigma^{-1/2}(r - \hat{r})\|_2 \implies \|u\|_{\mathcal{G}^*} = \|\Sigma^{1/2} u\|_2\).
  • Anisotropic Quantile-Mahalanobis ("quantile_mahalanobis", Blanchet, Kang & Murthy, 2019): Calibrates an anisotropic transport matrix \(\Sigma_{\text{tail}} = D_{\text{tail}} C_{\text{corr}} D_{\text{tail}}\) from the Riemann Bar inter-decile spread \((q_{0.90, i} - q_{0.10, i})\) and negative Bowley skewness \(\mathcal{S}_{\text{Bowley}, i}\): [ \left(D_{\text{tail}}\right){i,i} = \frac{1}{2}\left(\sigma_i + \frac{q} - q_{0.10, i}}{2.56 \sqrt{252}}\right)\sqrt{1 + \kappa_{\text{tail}} \max(0, -\mathcal{S{\text{Bowley}, i})}, \qquad |u| u\right|_2 ]}^*} = \left|\Sigma_{\text{tail}}^{1/2
  • Euclidean ("l2"): \(d(r, \hat{r}) = \|r - \hat{r}\|_2 \implies \|u\|_{\mathcal{G}^*} = \|u\|_2\).
  • Manhattan ("l1"): \(d(r, \hat{r}) = \|r - \hat{r}\|_1 \implies \|u\|_{\mathcal{G}^*} = \|u\|_\infty\).

docs.title: 2. Dynamic Bures-Wasserstein Radius Calibration
docs.text:
When radius_mode="regime_adaptive", the ambiguity radius \(\varepsilon_t\) scales dynamically with the Bures-Wasserstein \(W_2\) distance between fast and slow market covariance baths (via WassersteinRegimeGate):

\[ \varepsilon_t = \varepsilon_{\text{base}} + \kappa_{\text{regime}} \cdot W_2\!\left(\mathcal{N}(\mu_{\text{fast}}, \Sigma_{\text{fast}}), \, \mathcal{N}(\mu_{\text{slow}}, \Sigma_{\text{slow}})\right) \]

docs.title: 3. Wasserstein-Kelly Log-Growth Formulation (Li, 2023) & Fonseca-Junca Views (2021)
docs.text:
Given view-projected atoms \(\tilde{r}_i = r_i + \Sigma G^\top (G \Sigma G^\top)^{-1}(q - G \hat{\mu})\) and fractional Kelly parameter \(\eta \in (0, 1]\), the worst-case expected geometric log-growth program is solved as a single convex exponential-cone program over \((w, \lambda)\):

\[ \max_{w \in \mathcal{W}, \, \lambda \in \mathbb{R}^K} \; \sum_{i=1}^M p_i \ln\!\left(1 + \eta \, \tilde{r}_i^\top w\right) - \varepsilon_t \, \eta \, \|w - G^\top \lambda\|_{\mathcal{G}^*} - \rho_{\text{view}} \|\lambda\|_2^2 \]

For WASSERSTEIN_CVAR, the worst-case Expected Shortfall at confidence \(\beta\) reduces to:

\[ \min_{w \in \mathcal{W}, \, \alpha, \, s \ge 0, \, \lambda} \; \alpha + \frac{1}{1 - \beta}\left(\sum_{i=1}^M p_i s_i + \varepsilon_t \|w - G^\top \lambda\|_{\mathcal{G}^*}\right) + \rho_{\text{view}} \|\lambda\|_2^2 \quad \text{s.t.} \quad s_i \ge -\tilde{r}_i^\top w - \alpha \]

docs.title: References & Papers
docs.text: PyAlloq's algorithms are grounded in seminal academic research. This page provides full citations, summaries, and links to the papers that inspired each component.

docs.title: Markowitz (1952) — Portfolio Selection
docs.text:
Markowitz, H. (1952). Portfolio Selection. The Journal of Finance, 7(1), 77–91. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1540-6261.1952.tb01525.x

Contribution: Foundational mean-variance framework. Introduced the concept of the efficient frontier — the set of portfolios offering maximum expected return for a given level of risk.

Key formula: [ \min_w w^\top \Sigma w \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \mu^\top w = \mu^*, \; \mathbf{1}^\top w = 1 ]

Implemented in: MarkowitzAllocator (MIN_VOLATILITY, MAX_SHARPE, MAX_RETURN)

docs.title: Maillard, Roncalli & Teïletche (2010) — Equal Risk Contributions
docs.text:
Maillard, S., Roncalli, T., & Teïletche, J. (2010). The Properties of Equally Weighted Risk Contributions Portfolios. The Journal of Portfolio Management, 36(4), 60–70. https://doi.org/10.3905/jpm.2010.36.4.060

Contribution: Defined the Equal Risk Contribution (ERC) portfolio — a practical middle ground between Equal Weight and Minimum Variance. Showed that ERC portfolios can be computed via a convex optimization problem.

Key formula: [ w_i (\Sigma w)_i = w_j (\Sigma w)_j \quad \forall i, j ]

Implemented in: RiskParityAllocator, RiskBudgetingAllocator

docs.title: Choueifaty & Coignard (2008) — Maximum Diversification
docs.text:
Choueifaty, Y., & Coignard, Y. (2008). Toward Maximum Diversification. The Journal of Portfolio Management, 35(1), 40–51. https://doi.org/10.3905/JPM.2008.35.1.40

Contribution: Introduced the Diversification Ratio as a measure of portfolio diversification. The Maximum Diversification portfolio maximizes this ratio.

Key formula: [ D(w) = \frac{w^\top \sigma}{\sqrt{w^\top \Sigma w}} ]

Implemented in: MaxDiversificationAllocator

docs.title: López de Prado (2016) — Hierarchical Risk Parity
docs.text:
López de Prado, M. (2016). Building Diversified Portfolios that Outperform Out-of-Sample. The Journal of Portfolio Management, 42(4), 59–69. https://doi.org/10.3905/jpm.2016.42.4.059 arXiv:1603.05831

Contribution: Proposed HRP — a machine learning approach to portfolio construction that avoids covariance matrix inversion. Uses hierarchical clustering and recursive bisection to allocate weights in a tree-like structure.

Steps: Distance matrix → Hierarchical clustering → Quasi-diagonalization → Recursive bisection

Implemented in: HRPAllocator

docs.title: Black & Litterman (1992) — Global Portfolio Optimization
docs.text:
Black, F., & Litterman, R. (1992). Global Portfolio Optimization. Financial Analysts Journal, 48(5), 28–43. https://doi.org/10.2469/faj.v48.n5.28

Contribution: Combined CAPM equilibrium returns with subjective investor views through Bayesian updating. Produces more stable and intuitive return estimates than pure historical means.

Key formula: [ \mu^* = \left[(\tau\Sigma)^{-1} + P^\top \Omega^{-1} P\right]^{-1} \left[(\tau\Sigma)^{-1} \Pi + P^\top \Omega^{-1} Q\right] ]

Implemented in: BlackLittermanEstimator

docs.title: Das et al. (2024), Mistral AI (2026) & Potapczynski et al. (2026) — Time-Series Foundation Models & Prior-Data Fitted Networks (TimesFM-3, Timestral & ApolloPFN)

Potapczynski, A., Selvam, R. K., Konstantinova, T., Wolff, M., Olivares, K. G., Ma, R., Mahoney, M. W., Wilson, A. G., Oreshkin, B. N., & Efimov, D. (2026). Time-Aware Prior Fitted Networks for Zero-Shot Forecasting with Exogenous Variables (ApolloPFN). Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR, 06/2026). https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2603.15802

Hollmann, N., Müller, S., Purucker, L., Krishnakumar, A., Körfer, M., Hoo, S. B., Schirrmeister, R. T., & Hutter, F. (2025). Accurate predictions on small data with a tabular foundation model (TabPFN-v2). Nature, 637, 319–326.
